item.title: 38 Years Later, Calvin and Hobbes' Lost Character Remains Bill Watterson's Biggest Failure
item.description: The author Lois McMaster Bujold has said that “the writer should always reserve the right to come up with a better idea.” That's a useful guideline for any reader to keep in mind. As any long-form story evolves, it usually picks up a few dead plot branches or abandoned characters , because the author can exercise their option to drop what they're doing for any (or no) reason. Sometimes it's not a continuity error; it's a deliberate change in direction.

item.title: 3 takeaways as Victor Wembanyama's double-double leads Spurs to seventh straight win
item.description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) defends Sacramento Kings forward Domantas Sabonis (11) during the first half of an NBA basketball game on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Sacramento, Calif. (AP Photo/Jose Luis Villegas) (Jose Luis Villegas/Associated Press) SACRAMENTO, Calif. - Victor Wembanyama cooled off a bit, but it didn't stop him from leading his team to yet another win. Wembanyama finished with 30 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks, Stephon Castle had 19 points and a team-high seven assists, and the Spurs crushed the Sacramento Kings 124-109 Friday night for their seventh straight win in the opening game of NBA Cup group play for both teams. The Spurs' winning streak is the longest in the league this season. Wembanyama's modest - by his standards - stat line came after his 52-point, 24-rebound, eight-block masterpiece in a 112-111 victory over Dallas on Wednesday night at the Frost Bank Center. "I expect Victor to play the right way," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said when asked if there was a minimum amount of points he expects his star player to produce each game. "He obviously has a tremendous amount of gravity in terms of putting the defense in a tough spot when he's putting pressure on the rim and running the floor and rolling after screens. And I think that's going to produce points, but there are teams that have made very concerned efforts at times of taking that away. And what that should do then is open up opportunities for his teammates." That happened against the Kings in the form of Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell scoring 19 points each on a night the Spurs hit 15 of 30 shots from 3-point range. "We've got a team well-built," Wembanyama said. Said Harper, "We're at our best when everyone's touching the ball, everyone's getting to the paint, kicking out, just making the right play. And it's just a byproduct of our chemistry and how much we generally enjoy playing with each other." Playing on the first night of a back-to-back that ends in Portland and the first outing of a four-game road trip, the Spurs (7-2) took a 19-point lead into halftime Friday after Wembanyama scored 20 points and eight rebounds. Playing 26 minutes overall, he finished 10 of 18 from the field and 4 of 6 from beyond the arc. With his fourth 30-point game of the season and seventh double-double, Wembanyama joined Shaquille O'Neal (1993-94) and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (1975-76) as the only players to post 250 points, 100 rebounds and 35 blocks in the first nine games of a season since blocks became official (1973-74). Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. tallied 22 points on an inefficient 9-of-20 from the field to lead the Kings, who fell to 1-8 with their second loss in a row. Domantas Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and five assists for Sacramento. The start of the game was delayed for about 20 minutes due to a mechanical issue with the basket the Spurs shot at during warm-ups. item.title: Sebastian Tounekti’s Celtic difficulty
item.description: Sebastian Tounekti’s Celtic difficulty It’s hard to see a way back for Sebastian Tounekti at Celtic, with Jota and Yang now available and Callum Osmand likely to remain as a wide player, a January move could well be on the cards for the Tunisian…. 11th October 2026; Fir Park, Motherwell, North Lanarkshire, Scotland; Scottish Premiership Football, Motherwell versus Celtic; Sebastian Tounekti of Celtic Sebastian Tounekti continues to frustrate the Celtic supporters and it was clear on Thursday evening that the support’s patience is wearing very thin indeed when it comes to the Tunisian international winger. At this moment in time it’s hard to see a way back for the Tounekti, with a January move most likely on the cards, foe an number of reasons including of course the return to the squad of both Jota and Yang and both you would expect would be ahead of Seb in the pecking order. 1st November 2026; Falkirk Stadium, Scottish Premiership, Falkirk versus Celtic; Camilo Duran of Celtic and Sebastian Tounekti of Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou The 24 year old was signed by Brendan Rodgers in the summer of 2025 in a £5 million deal from Swedish side Hammarby, and despite showing some signs of promise he’s failed to show that he’s worth a regular run in the Celtic side. Listen, I’m all for giving players a chance, and I like many other supporters gave Seb that opportunity, but he’s failed to convince us that he has a long term future at the club. Some have even described Seb as the ‘Tunisian Mikey Johnston’ and I can understand why. Great on his day, and you could make him look like a world beater on a YouTube compilation. But the reality is that he’s a player who flatters to deceive, with his goal contributions limited to low numbers. 11th October 2026; Fir Park, Scottish Premiership, Motherwell versus Celtic; Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates with Sebastian Tounekti of Celtic after he shoots and scores in the 9th minute to make it 1-0. Photo by Vagelis Georgariou There’s a reason that Seb isn’t a regular in the starting XI, and whether that was Brendan Rodgers, Wilfried Nancy or Martin O’Neill, they all held or hold the same opinion of the Tunisian, and that would be that none of them rate him that highly. Seb is your classic ‘ impact’ player in my opinion, but is far from being a regular starter for Celtic. Bring him on when you need some fresh legs and creativity, but even then he’s still failing to impress despite having the ability to do so. Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with Benjamin Nygren of Celtic and Callum Osmand of Celtic during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) With Callum Osmand impressing out wide, Martin O’Neill sees the former Fulham youngster as a more viable option despite him being a centre forward by trade, so that speaks volumes for Martin O’Neill’s feelings regarding the Tunisian. item.title: ‘Some legends don't say goodbye’: Ex-India cricketer's heartfelt message for Mohammed Shami after Test retirement
item.description: Former India cricketer and ex-Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary paid an emotional tribute to Mohammed Shami after the veteran fast bowler announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 12-year career in the longest format. Tiwary, who had the opportunity to lead Bengal with Shami in his bowling attack, took to X to reflect on the pacer's impact and recall his association with the speedster. He described Shami as a warrior, while also highlighting the lasting memories he had created through his performances in the red-ball format. "The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history," Tiwary wrote. — tiwarymanoj (@tiwarymanoj) Recalling his time as Bengal captain, he added: "This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart" Shami's announcement brings an end to an impressive Test career spanning 64 matches, during which he picked up 229 wickets. The 36-year-old made the announcement through an Instagram post, confirming that while he would no longer represent India in the white jersey, he intended to continue playing white-ball cricket. "I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote. "Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added. A 12-year journey in India's Test colours Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. His ability to extract movement through seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a crucial member of India's pace attack across different conditions. Of his 229 wickets, 131 came in 35 Tests played in South Africa, the West Indies and India, where he maintained an average of under 25. South Africa witnessed some of Shami's finest performances in Test cricket. During India's 2018 tour, he produced a match-winning spell of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test, helping the visitors secure a consolation victory. On India's subsequent visit to the country, he continued his impressive record by claiming eight wickets in the series-opening Test at Centurion. Shami's final appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's. Injuries later disrupted his career, and he remained out of the Indian team after the 2025 Champions Trophy, before deciding to bring his red-ball journey to a close.

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives two match points to end Taylor Fritz's ATP Finals hopes
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz survived two match points against Taylor Fritz to book a spot in the last four of the Paris Masters and end his opponent’s hopes of reaching the ATP Finals. In a lengthy contest that lasted two hours and 43 minutes, the second seed lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3. Had Fritz taken one of his opportunities in the second set, he would have locked down the eighth and last place in the end-of-year championship. Instead, that spot now goes to Alcaraz’s fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar. After being outlasted by Fritz in the opener, Alcaraz had to save match points with and against serve in the second, before levelling the scores with three games in a row. He belatedly took control as he closed out the decider in clinical fashion. Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges await the Spaniard in the semi-finals. “I tried not to let myself down in the difficult moments in the second set,” Alcaraz said. Carlos Alcaraz is into the semi-finals of the Paris Masters (Getty) “I tried to stay strong mentally and save those break points and match points. I used the people and the energy and gave them what they really wanted to watch. “I am really happy to play for one and a half hours more to entertain them. The feeling I have today is unmatched.”

item.title: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report
item.description: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that have affected the team this season. According to SPORT , sporting director Deco is examining several possibilities, although the club’s limited financial flexibility in January means finding an affordable reinforcement will be a significant challenge. Barcelona decided against recruiting a central defender during the summer, directing their resources towards strengthening midfield and attack instead. However, an accumulation of defensive injuries exposed the squad’s lack of depth, increasing the urgency to reinforce the position before the second half of the season. Given Barcelona’s financial condition, Deco is exploring loans, affordable transfers and opportunities involving players whose contractual situations could make them accessible. Fikayo Tomori and Vitor Reis among Barcelona’s defensive options On that note, AC Milan’s Fikayo Tomori is one of the leading names under consideration. The English defender’s contract expires in 2027, and Milan are reportedly open to negotiating his departure in January. Interest from several Premier League clubs could nevertheless create competition for his signature. Barcelona are keeping tabs on Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images) Manchester City’s Vitor Reis is another possibility . The Brazilian has struggled for regular opportunities, accumulating just 199 minutes across four appearances this season. A temporary move could offer him valuable playing time, although there is no indication that City are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the season. Piero Hincapie also attracts Barcelona’s attention because of his versatility. The Ecuadorian can operate at both centre-back and left-back, making him particularly suitable for Flick’s defensive requirements. In fact, Deco has already sounded out his representatives about a potential loan with an option to buy. Lisandro Martinez and Lucas Beraldo offer different possibilities Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez is considered another attractive option . His contract situation, experience and ability on the ball make him an interesting candidate, although negotiating with United would not necessarily be easy. Lucas Beraldo’s situation at PSG could result in a January exit. (Photo by Francesco Scaccianoce/Getty Images) Furthermore, Paris Saint-Germain’s Lucas Beraldo has also emerged on the reported shortlist. The Brazilian’s technical qualities and suitability for a possession-oriented defensive system appeal to Barcelona, while his limited involvement under Luis Enrique could potentially create an opportunity. item.title: New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final
item.description: Stacey Waaka has represented New Zealand in rugby sevens, rugby union and rugby league [Getty Images] New Zealand (8) 32 Tries: Wiki, Waaka 3, Hufanga, Atai, McGregor Goals: Kiria-Ratu 2 Samoa (0) 0 New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final. It will be the Kiwi Ferns' seventh successive appearance in the showpiece match, but having won the first three between 2000-2008, three trips to the final since then have all ended in heartache. Three consecutive losses to Australia included a blowout 54-4 scoreline four years ago at Old Trafford and unless debutants Fiji spring one of the greatest upsets in the tournament's history in the other semi-final, the Jillaroos are likely to again provide the substantial obstacle to New Zealand becoming four-time champions. However, on Saturday, New Zealand made light of the blustery and difficult conditions inside Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, to make their case as potential winners. Mackenzie Wiki's try - less than two minutes into proceedings, off the back of a Samoa error - set the tone for the Kiwi Ferns. As the storm clouds began to gather overhead, New Zealand's dual-code international Stacey Waaka capitalised on some indecision from Samoa winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala to collect and ground Raecene McGregor's kick. It was efficient and highly professional from New Zealand, who conceded just 24 points across their three group games and once again exhibited their defensive parsimony during a hard-fought first period. A combination of that and Samoa's inability to make the most of field position, with a smattering of handling errors thrown in as well, laid the platform for New Zealand's triumph. There were notable bright spots for the Samoa fans to enjoy. Fanua Rimoni was a powerful and dominant presence at lock forward, while teenage winger Anastasia Leatupue produced a nerveless showing on her international bow. Samoa's biggest disappointment was that they could not get the ball into the hands of the 18-year-old in good attacking positions - with Pauline Piliae-Rasabale twice pulled up for forward passes on the right edge in an error-strewn display. But just like in the first 35 minutes, they had no answer to New Zealand's more potent attacking threat. Waaka was again the beneficiary of a pinpoint McGregor kick as she crossed for her second try and Mele Hufanga held off the attentions of three Samoa defenders tfor her score. It was a feat that was matched by Kaiyah Atai just over two minutes later as New Zealand went through the gears. With Samoa's resistance gradually waning, Waaka capped a fine individual display with her hat-trick and McGregor scored the try her performance richly deserved to round off a fine New Zealand display. item.title: Paraguay Senate impeaches President Peña, VP Alliana takes over
item.description: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts. Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links. Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent. Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment. “Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP. Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters. Alliana promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno Bank’s takeover amid insolvency concerns. “Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated,” said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. Opposition lawmakers had also filed a motion to impeach Alliana over the crisis, but the request failed to gain congressional approval. – Money trickles back – The bank’s demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno. Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, a Central Bank official told AFP. The first phase of aid deposits, up to around $1,600, will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, said Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund. The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he added. Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that have stripped him of political immunity. The opposition accused the US-backed politician of a conflict of interest, which he denied. The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.” He will be questioned over alleged crimes of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds on Saturday, prosecutor Gonzalez Vester said. Pena urged reconciliation in an X post shortly before his removal. “Today, we must come together as Paraguayans to rebuild our institutions and restore trust,” he said. The US Embassy in Paraguay expressed “its solidarity with the Paraguayan people” on Friday, without mentioning the president. – ‘Pena in prison’ – “Pena in prison,” read one of the protest signs outside Congress on Friday. item.title: 24 ‘pointless races’ in 10 years: Formula 1 has an end-of-season problem
item.description: Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP’s final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year’s Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi . Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective. Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton ’s all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit. Verstappen lost out in last year's title showdown with Lando Norris (Getty) But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers’ title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport’s ultimate prize on the line. There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory. This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness. Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the “battle for second” or the “best of the rest” tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that. Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten. item.title: Islam Makhachev Drops Major Hint About Retirement, Could Follow Khabib Nurmagomedov’s Lead
item.description: Islam Makhachev’s future in the UFC has been a major talking point over the past few days. The reigning welterweight champion drew plenty of criticism from fans and pundits after reportedly pulling out of negotiations for a fight at UFC 336 . Makhachev was initially expected to defend his 170-pound title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card. However, those plans fell apart after the Dagestani stepped away from the proposed matchup. The champion later explained that the welterweight division had several deserving contenders and believed Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate inside the Octagon. However, the fight negotiations aren’t the only reason Makhachev’s future has come under scrutiny. The two-division champion recently turned 35 on October 27 and has openly discussed the possibility of retirement. He has suggested that he doesn’t have many fights left and wants to spend the remainder of his career facing the toughest available competition. Now, he has offered another hint that his retirement might be closer than expected. Islam Makhachev Says He Will Listen to His Mother When It Comes to UFC Retirement During a recent interview with Red Corner MMA in Tashkent, Makhachev suggested that his career could come to an end much like that of Khabib Nurmagomedov. Interestingly, their mothers could have a say in both decisions. For those unfamiliar, ‘The Eagle’ retired at 32 after promising his mother that he wouldn’t fight again without his father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Following Abdulmanap’s passing ahead of UFC 254, ‘The Eagle’ decided to honor that promise . The Dagestani went on to secure his 29th professional victory against Justin Gaethje in Abu Dhabi before announcing his retirement inside the Octagon. Makhachev now appears to be considering a similar path. He said, “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” The former lightweight champion also admitted that he doesn’t have a specific number of fights in mind before calling it a day. However, he made it clear that he feels his career is nearing its end. Islam Makhachev hints he will soon follow his mother’s wish for him to stop fighting. 🥺 “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” https://t.co/PKryqIPJSc — Red Corner MMA (@RedCorner_MMA) November 6, 2026 ALSO READ: Ilia Topuria Hails Alexander Volkanovski as UFC’s Greatest Featherweight, Rules Out Rematch Makhachev added, “There’s no number. I am just reaching the finish line. There aren’t many things that could give me motivation in this sport. I’m at the finish line. I just want to fight the contenders, but I don’t see any new names.” Interestingly, many would argue that Prates and Morales are exactly the kind of fresh challenges Makhachev is looking for. item.title: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star
item.description: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star Manchester United have not started the 2026/2027 season in any way, shape or form as they would have imagined in August. Season The Red Devils currently sit 17th in the league and have only won one match out of nine. What’s more, they have been dumped out of the League Cup and have won two and lost two of their Champions League matches so far. United signed Senne Lammens last season from Royal Antwerp and he hugely impressed in the United goal, marking a big step up from Andre Onana or Altay Bayindir. Nonetheless, this season has been more of a challenge and even though he has not made many big errors, he has conceded too many goals for a United keeper. Marco Carnesecchi links Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb have jumped on this possible dissatisfaction with the job Lammens is currently doing and linked the club to Atalanta’s Marco Carnesecchi. The outlet states, “Marco Carnesecchi is on Manchester United’s radar.” The site continues, the “Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi has caught Manchester United’s eye. The Reds are keen to sign the Nerazzurri player as a backup, partly based on his performances in recent months.” Tuttomercatoweb also claim, “while Senne Lammens was excellent during his first season—even winning awards for his performances—he has now conceded 23 goals in 13 matches, with only one clean sheet to his name so far, against Sabah.” United could even look to do a deal for the Italian as early as January, according to the site. One potential complexity is that the keeper signed a deal in the spring which keeps him contracted at the club until 2030. Nonetheless, “a significant contract extension, though one that might not necessarily put an end to the Red Devils’ pursuit—even if the fee demanded by Atalanta is far from low.” What’s more, “it is clear that the ups and downs of this season in Bergamo could make a potential departure more likely,” even if Atalanta have little history in selling their top stars in the winter market. Carnesecchi has played 15 matches this season in all competitions, conceding 25 goals and keeping three clean sheets. Why? ⚠️ Whilst Lammens has been far from impressive, Carnesecchi’s record is hardly better ⚠️ With limited funds and needs in defence and attack, United are unlikely to spend on a goalkeeper in January TPP view We believe that Manchester United have limited funds for January and currently have much greater needs than improving the goalkeeping situation. item.title: Windows takes a break at UK motorway services
item.description: A roadside display at Cherwell Valley services has stopped dispensing information and started asking for help. The eagle-eyed Register reader who spotted the stricken screen told us: "UK motorway signs often tell us that tiredness can kill, urging us to take a break. This poor thing at Cherwell Valley services took the advice to heart." The display at the Moto services appears to have run into trouble during a restart. Windows offers another attempt or access to repair tools, although the latter options are hidden – perhaps somewhere on the top floor of the neighboring Travelodge. Getting things moving again will probably require access to the computer behind the screen. The Automatic Repair screen is all too familiar to Windows users. Not to be confused with the classic blue screen of death, it might indicate a misbehaving driver during a reboot, an update that did something unexpected, or some sort of hardware failure. Hopefully it isn't the latter – with memory and storage prices the way they are at the moment, a motorway services sandwich or gallon of fuel will seem a positive bargain by comparison. Our reader is right: taking a break is sensible advice. Getting Windows to end one can be another matter. ®

item.title: Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory
item.description: The mayor of Houston, Texas announced Friday that the city’s police department will limit its cooperation with federal immigration agents after Democrats swept midterm elections this week. The so-called “blue tsunami” ousted Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Texas ally of US President Donald Trump, who has cracked down on immigration with raids conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents since returning to office last year. Abbott had threatened in April to revoke $110 million in public safety funding from Houston if city officials didn’t walk back a similar measure earlier this year, and city officials complied. He lost reelection on Tuesday and will be replaced by Democrat Gina Hinojosa, the first Latina woman elected governor of Texas. Now, Houston Mayor John Whitmire has signed an executive order instructing Houston police to not contact ICE agents when a person is detained for nonviolent offenses, like a traffic stop. “It’s to reduce the fear and anxiety, not just in some of our communities but across Houston,” Whitmire said during a press conference announcing the change. The 77-year-old mayor acknowledged that the change could bring some political risks but said he was ready to meet them, as Abbott and other Republicans remain in power until January. ICE released a statement on X reacting to the change, writing: “Watching child porn and selling heroin are classified as ‘nonviolent offenses’ by the way.” “This is the Mayor of Houston directly advocating for policies that protect some of the worst criminals in America,” it added. According to the Prison Policy Initiative, a nonpartisan think tank, Texas has had more arrests carried out by ICE agents during Trump’s second term than any other state, with almost 137,000 recorded as of August 2026. Texas is also the state with the highest number of ICE detainees in the US, with over 16,000 held at various facilities — more than double the amount held in the second highest state, Louisiana — according to Syracuse University’s Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. The post Houston mayor limits immigration agents cooperation by police after Democratic victory appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lakers rally past Blazers behind Dončić’s 53 points
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts after hitting a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against Portland Trailblazers, Friday, November 6, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — Luka Dončić gave the Lakers a chance before halftime with a shot from beyond half court. In the third quarter, he helped turn that chance into control. Dončić scored a season-high 53 points, including 20 in the third quarter, as the Lakers overcame a 16-point deficit to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 124-118 on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers improved to 8-2 with their fourth straight win, avenging their Oct. 27 loss to Portland and earning their first NBA Cup win of the season. It was Dončić’s fourth 50-point regular-season game as a Laker and the 11th of his career. He has scored 361 points through his first nine games this season, the most since Wilt Chamberlain scored 472 (insane!) through nine games in 1962-63, according to the Lakers. Dončić is now at an average of 40.1 points per game which ranks third in NBA history through a player’s first nine games of a season, behind only Chamberlain’s starts in 1962-63 (52.4) and 1961-62 (50.6), according to the team. “For now ... I don’t have any words,” coach JJ Redick said of Dončić’s historic scoring surge. Austin Reaves recovered from missing his first seven shots to finish with 25 points. Walker Kessler added 16 points and 12 rebounds, while Dončić contributed five rebounds and five assists. The Lakers needed much of that production after an opening quarter in which they missed all 12 of their 3-point attempts. Portland made six of its 12 attempts from deep, building a 29-20 lead despite Dončić supplying half of L.A.’s points. Redick had called an early timeout with Portland ahead 10-4 and the Lakers shooting 2 for 12 overall. The deficit eventually reached 16 in the second quarter, with Reaves unable to find his first basket until a runner ended his 0-for-7 start. Still, Redick saw reasons to trust the offense. The shots began to fall toward the end of the second quarter that ended in Dončić's longest bucket of the season. Dončić banked in a heave from beyond half court at the buzzer (and I GOT IT!), cutting Portland’s lead to 60-53. The Lakers entered halftime within seven despite shooting 4 for 23 from 3-point range. Luka Doncic at the buzzer from half court and the #Lakers are now down seven, 60-53, at the half. Luka has 20 points. pic.twitter.com/z3Vp0gN3MY — Carlos Yakimowich (@CarlosYakJr) November 7, 2026 “I thought it was an important shot to make. So that’s why I decided to make it,” Dončić said. He carried that momentum into the third quarter. The Lakers used a 20-8 run to move ahead 73-68, with Dončić scoring 11 points during that stretch. They went on to outscored Portland 34-15 in the period, taking an 87-75 lead into the fourth. Portland made another push, but Dončić delivered a jumper in the lane with 28 seconds remaining to help protect the advantage. L.A. also created ext

item.title: Steelers-Chargers Trade Idea Swaps Former 3rd-Round Pick for 1,000-Yard WR
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 01: Roman Wilson #14 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a 12 yard touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers could get Aaron Rodgers another proven receiver before the NFL trade deadline, but one proposed deal would come at the expense of a young wideout and a valuable draft pick. The proposed trade would send Roman Wilson to the Los Angeles Chargers, where he would reunite with former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh. In return, Pittsburgh would land a receiver who surpassed 1,000 yards as a rookie and could become a long-term piece of its offense. Steelers-Chargers Trade Proposal Sends Roman Wilson for Ladd McConkey In a look at four potential Steelers trades, CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo proposed Pittsburgh acquiring Ladd McConkey and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Chargers in exchange for Wilson and a 2027 second-round selection. The deal would give Pittsburgh an established receiver while sending Wilson back to the coach he played under during Michigan’s national championship season. “It’s possible that the Steelers wouldn’t have to part with Wilson in this scenario,” DeArdo wrote. However, he suggested the Chargers would likely want another receiver if they were willing to surrender McConkey, making Wilson an intriguing option because of his history with Harbaugh. Wilson caught 48 passes for 789 yards and 12 touchdowns during his final season at Michigan in 2023. He was a key part of the Wolverines’ undefeated championship run before Pittsburgh selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. His NFL career hasn’t followed the same trajectory. Injuries have limited his opportunities, although Wilson has recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five appearances this season. McConkey would bring considerably more notable production. The former Georgia standout caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns during his rookie season in 2024. He followed that with 66 receptions for 789 yards and six scores in 2025. Through six games this season, McConkey has 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown. Still, getting the Chargers to surrender one of their most productive young receivers would present a considerable challenge. “The Chargers also probably don’t want to part with McConkey,” DeArdo said. The proposed second-round pick could make the conversation more interesting, particularly with Wilson giving Harbaugh a familiar receiver to develop. Steelers Would Sacrifice Valuable Draft Pick for Ladd McConkey Pittsburgh’s need for another receiving threat has become difficult to ignore despite its 6-2 record and first-place standing in the AFC North. The Carolina Panthers are considering potential adjustments to their offensive line ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Denver Broncos . After struggling to keep quarterback Bryce Young protected in recent weeks, the coaching staff is assessing different options in an effort to put together a more dependable unit. ESPN senior NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler discussed Carolina’s ongoing offensive line problems on NFL Network, saying that the team is exploring ‘potential solutions’ to address its protection issues. “Bryce Young has had 11 sacks in the last two weeks,” Fowler said. “He was under constant duress in that Thursday night game against Green Bay. So he was asked about it today. He would not tip his hand on that, but I know they have at least evaluated that situation. “Part of the problem is they’ve been pretty beat up with injuries. There’s only so much they can do. Their left guard, Damien Lewis, is already out for the second straight week. So they might have to stand pat, but they are looking at potential solutions.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Carolina’s offensive line has endured significant difficulties throughout the season, with a series of injuries forcing the coaching staff to experiment with different combinations. The Panthers are now focused on identifying a lineup that can provide better protection for Young while also improving the team’s ability to establish a consistent running game. Beyond their offensive struggles, Carolina has also encountered major problems on the defensive side of the ball. Those issues have contributed to significant coaching changes, including the dismissals of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley . The challenge will be even greater against a Broncos team entering the matchup with a 6-2 record. Unless Carolina finds a way to shore up its protection, Young could be in for another difficult outing as the Panthers attempt to get their offense back on track. item.title: Devils stay top with overtime victory against Stars
item.description: Cardiff Devils wore a one-off bespoke uniform, with the game against Dundee Stars designated 'country night'. [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November. Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display. Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error. The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second. Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff. "It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson. "We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner." Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).

item.title: JJ Gabriel confirms he has picked Real Madrid over Barcelona
item.description: JJ Gabriel confirms he has picked Real Madrid over Barcelona Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel has indicated a clear preference for Real Madrid over Barcelona, dealing a blow to the Catalans’ attempts to secure one of English football’s most highly rated young talents. The recently turned 16-year-old attacker, who has attracted interest from several European clubs, made his position clear during an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca while visiting the Spanish capital. Asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid, Gabriel did not hesitate, saying: “Barcelona or Real Madrid? Obviously, Real Madrid.” The youngster also revealed his ambitions for the future, making clear that he has his sights set on the highest individual honours in football. “My dream is to win a Ballon d’Or,” he said. His comments come amid reports that a move to Real Madrid is progressing , with the transfer close to completion. Real Madrid move ahead after Barcelona withdraw from transfer race It is to be remembered that Barcelona had identified the teenager as one of the most exciting prospects available and held several meetings with his representatives through sporting director Deco. The Catalans attempted to convince the youngster that joining La Masia would offer the ideal environment for his development. However, the financial demands of the operation also complicated Barcelona’s pursuit, with the club eventually withdrawing from the competition. JJ Gabriel will sign for Real Madrid. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid have since moved into a stronger position, even reaching a verbal agreement with Gabriel over a potential move, with the intention of bringing him to the club during the January transfer window. Barcelona admitted defeat Barcelona were among a number of suitors, including Bayern Munich and PSG, who held talks with the player’s representatives, but the sporting directive offered by Real Madrid made all the difference. Indeed, it can be argued that Barcelona boasts a better youth academy, but financial considerations also made a big difference. item.title: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important”
item.description: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important” Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with the club bringing in a number of stars to bolster the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. One such player who arrived with high expectations at the Santiago Bernabeu was Marc Cucurella. The World Cup winner was expected to be the player who would improve Madrid’s squad the most in a position that has been problematic since Marcelo’s exit. Cucurella explains what makes playing for Real Madrid different Representing Los Blancos has come with expectations that have far exceeded what Marc Cucurella initially anticipated. The Spaniard has now reflected on the unique responsibility that comes with wearing the Madrid shirt. “Being a Real Madrid player means that every match against another team is hugely important to them, perhaps the biggest match of the year,” the Spanish international explained. Cucurella has talked about the challenges of playing for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Having spent years at Barcelona coming through La Masia ‘s ranks, Cucurella understands both perspectives. “When I used to play against Madrid, that week was special: everyone wanted to come and see you, and they wrote to you,” he recalled. “Ultimately, having the responsibility of winning every match is a wonderful thing and easy to handle.” Facing Real Madrid is always a big occasion for their opponents, but playing for Los Blancos is a whole different challenge. A responsibility Cucurella is learning to embrace Cucurella had a difficult start to life at Real Madrid but has come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella is embracing his new life in the Spanish capital. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) His performances have coincided with Los Blancos ‘ upturn in form, and the Spaniard has firmly established himself as Jose Mourinho’s first-choice left-back. Cucurella is also facing significant competition from Alvaro Carreras, who has done nothing wrong in the chances Mourinho has given him. Between them, the manager has two high-quality options who can start on any given day, and that is a luxury to have. Cucurella will hope to put in a good performance against Valencia later tonight as Madrid look to extend their winning run to eight games. It remains to be seen how the Spaniard fares over the course of the season and how the battle between him and Carreras pans out. Source: RMTV

item.title: The Daily Hilario: Open wide for some soccer!
item.description: DUNAJSKÁ STREDA, SLOVAKIA - AUGUST 13: (L-R) Younes Taha of FC Twente, Filip Blazek of DAC 1904 during the Conference League match between DAC 1904 v FC Twente at the MOL Arena Dunajska Streda on August 13, 2026 in Dunajská Streda Slovakia (Photo by Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matchweek 10 is upon us in the Premier League — Everton beat Frank Lampard’s Coventry City last night, 3-1, to get it started already — and it’s the last one for a couple weeks as the international break shall follow after Sunday. item.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a heartfelt gesture Friday, honoring franchise legend Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday. LaFleur, who recently made a major quarterback change involving Gardner Minshew, arrived at his media availability wearing a shirt featuring the late safety. The maroon shirt featured an image of Tillman wearing his No. 40 Cardinals jersey, offering a simple but meaningful tribute photo to one of the organization’s most respected figures. Cardinals reporter Mark Dalton shared a photo of LaFleur’s tribute, highlighting the coach’s decision to commemorate Tillman’s milestone birthday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tillman, born November 6, 1976, played college football at Arizona State before joining the Cardinals in 1998. He spent four seasons with Arizona, establishing himself as a hard-hitting safety and earning widespread admiration for his dedication. Following the September 11 attacks, Tillman made the extraordinary decision to leave professional football and enlist in the United States Army alongside his brother Kevin. He served as an Army Ranger before passing away in Afghanistan on April 22, 2004, at just 27 years old. His legacy remains deeply connected to the Cardinals, who retired his No. 40 jersey and erected a statue outside State Farm Stadium in his honor. The tribute came as LaFleur prepared Arizona for its upcoming matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, with the Cardinals navigating significant roster changes after Jacoby Brissett’s departure to the Baltimore Ravens. Despite the demands of preparing for another divisional contest, LaFleur took time to recognize a figure whose influence extends well beyond football. His shirt served as another reminder that Tillman’s sacrifice and legacy continue to resonate throughout the Cardinals organization. item.title: Franco Colapinto Drives the Alpine-Themed Renault 6 Fans Took From Argentina to Brazil
item.description: Franco Colapinto made the hard work of his fans worthwhile by driving their custom Alpine themed Renault-6. (Source: MEGA, @ColapintoFiles/X) Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had restored a 1977 Renault 6 and decorated it with Alpine’s signature blue, pink and white colors, along with Colapinto’s racing number 43. Their remarkable journey from Esperanza, Santa Fe, to Brazil covered more than 2,000 kilometers. The three fans, Hernán Bonvín, Claudio Goddio and Pablo Quaino, had set out on the adventure with the dream of meeting their Formula 1 hero. After spotting the uniquely decorated car, Colapinto greeted the group with a smile and took a closer look at their creation. What followed was an unforgettable surprise as the Alpine driver climbed behind the wheel and took the Renault 6 for a drive through the streets of São Paulo. View this post on Instagram Videos of the encounter quickly spread across social media, capturing Colapinto enjoying the experience while the excited fans cheered from inside the vehicle. The Argentine even joked about the car’s radio system, asking whether it worked as he drove, prompting laughter from his passengers. The light-hearted interaction offered a memorable glimpse of the connection between the young driver and his supporters. Seeing Colapinto drive the car they had worked months on to get going made it all worth their while. The car, which they named ‘Renoleta ‘, became an eye-catching wonder wherever it went. It became an even more significant deal for the Argentine driver during the Brazilian GP weekend, as it highlighted the enthusiasm of South American F1 supporters. Franco Colapinto Has Reignited Argentina's F1 Passion Colapinto has rapidly become one of the most well-known young faces in Argentine motorsport, and his arrival in F1 has certainly rekindled the passion for the sport in Argentina. (Source: MEGA) The 23-year-old’s rising profile is also a reflection of the renewed interest in F1 amongst the Argentine fans, who have taken him as an ambassador for their country in the world of motorsport. item.title: Mika Baur on the demands of playing for Celtic
item.description: Mika Baur on the demands of playing for Celtic Mika Baur is slowly but surely getting used to the incredible demands of playing for Celtic. The German international spoke after his best performance so far on Thursday night’s victory over Besiktas in the Europa League… Mika Baur of Celtic passes the ball during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) The German international has spoke of the demands of playing three times a week, but is adamant he’s enjoying the hectic schedule. Baur getting used to Celtic’s intense playing schedule “To play every three days is different for me,” the midfielder said, to the mainstream media after Celtic’s 3-2 victory over Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday evening. “I think I have played the same amount of games now that I had last season by the winter break. Mika Baur of Celtic during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Celtic FC and Real Club Celta Vigo at Celtic Park on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) “But I like it. That’s what you want. You want to play all the time, more playing than training. I am really enjoying it. And I think the pressure to win is a good kind of pressure. It’s better than (trying) not to lose. So I really enjoy it,” Baur stated, as reported by Scottish Sun. “First of all, I want to work hard for the team, for myself, that I can prove myself and I can play on the stage, help the team, put in a shift, hard work,” he said. Baur impressed once again in the 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas , and not just due to his skill and technical ability but his overall pressing and battling attributes as the hoops fought to a hard earned win. “I was really happy that it was appreciated,” Mika Baur Mika Baur of Celtic is crowded out by Dundee United players Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock He added: “That’s what I have to do first. And then after this, the skill comes, playing with the ball. But first of all, it’s showing heart on the field. I was really happy that it was appreciated. “The second half was pure heart, pure fight,” Baur said. “I’m not here for a long time, but I think that’s what it’s all about. This win feels unbelievable because we deserved it. We fought for it. “The team is really, really close together. We know that we had a tough couple of weeks, but you can feel it in the training sessions, how the team is working together, the feeling, the believing is always there. Baur acknowledges the Celtic support – “They gave us a lot of energy” “And it was there on the pitch. That’s what we have to show week by week, every three days. “It was not just our win. The atmosphere was great. I’m really, really thankful for every supporter in the stadium. They gave us a lot of energy. We all fight together. That makes me happy.” Callum McGregor of Celtic applauds the fans

item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli The 2. Bundesliga serves up an interesting encounter this weekend as 1. FC Magdeburg welcome FC St. Pauli to the Avnet Arena. The hosts have made an impressive start to the campaign, particularly on home soil, and will be looking to strengthen their position in the promotion picture. Meanwhile, St. Pauli arrive in Saxony-Anhalt hoping to bounce back from last weekend's disappointing defeat to Nürnberg and end their remarkable run of away draws. With both sides having ambitions of challenging towards the top end of the table, Sunday's meeting promises to be an intriguing contest. 1. FC Magdeburg Magdeburg head into Sunday's encounter sitting fifth in the standings with 17 points from their opening ten matches, having established themselves as one of the division's most dangerous attacking sides. Petrik Sander's team were held to a 1-1 draw away to Darmstadt last weekend, with Tobias Müller giving the visitors an early lead before the hosts restored parity. Although the result prevented Magdeburg from making further ground on the leading sides, their overall performances have been encouraging, particularly at the Avnet Arena. Indeed, Magdeburg currently boast the joint-best home record in the division, having collected 12 points from their five home fixtures, scoring 15 goals in the process. Four victories from those matches underline the difficulty Sunday's visitors will face. Their attacking output has also been particularly impressive, with 21 goals scored across their opening ten league matches. Emmanuel Iyoha and Mateusz Żukowski have been especially influential, contributing 11 goals between them. However, Sander is refusing to underestimate the challenge posed by St. Pauli, despite their recent defeat to Nürnberg. Speaking ahead of the encounter, the Magdeburg coach described the visitors as a confident team and dismissed the idea that last weekend's performance would necessarily be repeated. Sander also highlighted St. Pauli's dominance against Nürnberg, suggesting that the 3-1 scoreline did not accurately reflect the balance of play. Magdeburg will therefore need to be at their best if they are to maintain their impressive home record and continue their push towards the promotion places. FC St. Pauli St. Pauli travel to Magdeburg looking to respond after suffering a disappointing 3-1 home defeat to Nürnberg last weekend. Despite enjoying lengthy spells of possession and creating several promising opportunities, Marcel Rapp's side were ultimately punished for their lack of efficiency in front of goal, conceding twice late in the contest. The result leaves the Hamburg outfit eighth in the standings with 12 points, having recorded just two victories from their opening ten league matches. item.title: Non-league's greatest giant-killers eye another scalp
item.description: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day." The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. Because despite twice winning what was then the Alliance Premier League, Altrincham were victims of a ballot system that cruelly denied them progression to the Football League - by just a single vote in 1980 - before automatic promotion was introduced a few years later. Heathcote scored a penalty against Liverpool in the FA Cup in 1981 [Getty Images] 'We have a real opportunity' Heathcote had left by the time Altrincham pulled off their greatest cup exploit - knocking out first division Birmingham City at St Andrews in 1986 in what remains one of the competition's biggest shocks. They became only the second of four non-league teams to beat top-flight opposition away from home. Fort

item.title: ‘Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm’ As Simon and Garfunkel never sang…
item.description: Simon and Garfunkel Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled “The Phoney War” , it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Newcastle United season. In September I contributed “All Things Bright and Beautiful” , about our promising start to the season. October’s article “Trick or Treat” arrived a little late last weekend. It raised doubts about how things are unfolding after a series of sloppy defeats. My offering this month? Fire and darkness. November starts with the dispiriting onset of darkness. As Simon and Garfunkel never sang, “Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm.” Darkness aside, there’s been more futility than fire from our footballing favourites. Maybe we’ll see a spark from Newcastle United in West London on Saturday. As the Scots say, maybe so, maybe no. Maybe we’ll see two bald men fighting over a comb. An increasingly dull, dreary and desperate attempt to win the coveted prize of being the fourth worst team in the league by the end of the season. There’s always hope , of course, the thing that kills you. We hope that Fulham will be even more wobbly than us. We hope that we can bag a fourth win of a mercurial season in the capital this weekend. We hope that the likes of Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich, Palace, Fulham will finish below us by the odd point or with a less embarrassing goal difference. We hope that Santa will bring us a little stocking filler in the form of a relegation berth for Man City. If so, we hope that we won’t be one of the other two trapdoor teams. We hope that it’s going to be alright. We hope Matthias Jaissle will turn it around. We hope that the Newcastle United players will get it. We hope there’s something for them to get. We hope for a couple of signings in January. We know all about hope as Newcastle supporters. We know the sorts of things we say in our brighter moments. But November darkness doesn’t encourage hope. There’s a beguiling song by an obscure folk singer Dave Goulder, entitled “The January Man”. It’s partly about the changing seasons, month by month. This month’s line is, “The poor November man sees fire and wind and mist and rain and winter air.” We can identify with that. So can our current manager, who looked like the poor November man at the end of Monday night’s match after shaking hands with the gargoyle Moyes. If you want a giggle in November’s darkness, search up “David Moyes Dunfermline”. It should bring up an image of a Soccer Stars/Panini type sticker of a young Davey Moyes in his playing days. Be warned: it belongs on the Halloween clearance shelf. Unsettling. NSFW. We might giggle but fly old Davey has demonstrated a certain brand of English football to MJ three times these last few months. As my Mam used to say, “that’ll learn him a thing or three.” Aggregate score 7-2. Gesundheit, or something that rhymes with it. item.title: Girona-Almeria: direct duel to get closer to the top part
item.description: Girona-Almeria: direct duel to get closer to the top part The Girona team returns to Montilivi to face a challenging match against UD Almeria, the second-placed team. After twelve rounds, the Andalusians have accumulated 26 points, while Girona has 21, a five-point difference that gives the match special significance in the fight to move closer to the top positions. Girona comes into the match after suffering a 1-0 defeat at the Real Sociedad B stadium. However, prior to that, they had achieved two convincing home victories: 2-0 against FC Andorra and 5-1 against Celta Fortuna. In the previous rounds, they also drew with Tenerife (1-1) and Mallorca (0-0). Their overall record stands at six wins, three draws, and three losses, with 22 goals scored and 11 conceded. Almeria, among the best in the category Almeria arrives at Montilivi with a solid trajectory: eight wins, two draws, and two losses in the first twelve rounds, with 23 goals scored and 10 conceded. In their last five matches, they have achieved three wins and two draws. Their most recent result was a 1-1 draw at Eibar's stadium. The Andalusian team boasts an offensive duo that has gained prominence in recent weeks. Miguel de la Fuente and Sergio Arribas have scored seven goals between them in the last five rounds. De la Fuente provides a strong presence in the area and finishing ability, while Arribas contributes creativity and attacking runs from midfield. Attention will also be needed for Brian Cipenga, who has scored three goals this season, and Thalys, who has netted two. Their contributions expand Almeria's offensive options and require Girona to stay focused against the various threats posed by their opponent.

item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Heidenheim vs. Hannover 96
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Heidenheim vs. Hannover 96 The 2. Bundesliga provides an intriguing encounter on the Ostalb, as Heidenheim get set to host Hannover. Both sides have experienced contrasting fortunes in recent weeks, with Heidenheim struggling to rediscover their early-season form, while Hannover will be looking to build on their first league victory under new head coach Sandro Wagner. With just four points separating the teams ahead of the 11th matchday, Sunday's meeting presents an important opportunity for both clubs to strengthen their position in the standings. 1. FC Heidenheim Heidenheim will be determined to get their promotion challenge back on track after suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Karlsruher SC last weekend. Frank Schmidt's side appeared to be heading towards a point after Alessandro Vogt equalised late in the contest, only for the hosts to snatch all three points with a stoppage-time winner. The result extended Heidenheim's winless run in the league to five matches, with their last victory coming against Holstein Kiel back in September. Despite their recent difficulties, the recently-relegated side remain sixth in the standings with 15 points from their opening ten fixtures. Their home form has also been a positive, with Schmidt's side unbeaten at the Voith-Arena this season, recording three victories and two draws from their five matches. Sunday's encounter also carries additional significance following Schmidt's announcement earlier this week that he will leave the club at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, bringing an end to his remarkable spell of almost 20 years in charge. Speaking ahead of the Hannover fixture, Schmidt acknowledged the quality within the opposition ranks but expects an intensely contested encounter. "Accordingly, Sunday will be a real battle," Schmidt explained, highlighting the importance of intensity, second balls and winning individual duels. The Heidenheim coach also admitted that his team had been overrun in certain situations during their defeat to Karlsruhe, insisting that his players needed to rediscover their sharpness in training before returning to home action. With their unbeaten home record on the line, Schmidt will be hoping his side can produce a response and return to winning ways. Hannover 96 Hannover travel to Heidenheim with renewed confidence after finally securing their first league victory under Sandro Wagner last weekend. The Lower Saxony outfit came from behind to defeat Dynamo Dresden 2-1, with Husseyn Chakroun and Marcel Hartel both scoring within seven second-half minutes to turn the contest around. The victory was particularly important following a difficult start to Wagner's tenure, which had seen Hannover struggle to translate their attacking potential into consistent results. item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: VfL Bochum vs. Karlsruher SC
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: VfL Bochum vs. Karlsruher SC The meeting presents an important opportunity for both sides to strengthen their positions in the 2. Bundesliga table as the season progresses. Bochum will be looking to make home advantage count, while Karlsruher SC travel to North Rhine-Westphalia hoping to come away with a positive result. VfL Bochum Bochum head into Sunday's encounter with renewed confidence after ending their difficult run of league form with a 2-1 victory away to Energie Cottbus last weekend. Uwe Rösler's side had endured a five-game winless run in the league before travelling to Cottbus, but Christian Rasmussen's late winner secured three valuable points and lifted the club to 11th in the standings. The victory was particularly important given Bochum's struggles in front of goal this season. Having scored just eight times in their opening ten league matches, they currently possess the lowest-scoring attack in the division. However, their recent cup victory over Mainz and the comeback success against Cottbus suggest that Rösler's team are beginning to find some momentum. Rösler is nevertheless expecting a difficult afternoon against a Karlsruhe side whose intensity and attacking movement could cause problems. Speaking ahead of the fixture, the Bochum coach described Sunday's encounter as a potential 50-50 contest and warned that the visitors are one of the most intense teams in the division. The German side will need to pay particular attention to Marvin Wanitzek, who Rösler identified as Karlsruhe's standout player, highlighting his ability to find space and influence matches through both open play and set-pieces. Karlsruher SC Karlsruher SC travel to Bochum looking to build on an encouraging 2-1 victory over 1. FC Heidenheim, which brought some much-needed stability to their start under new head coach Maximilian Senft. The Baden-Württemberg outfit had endured a difficult spell before welcoming Heidenheim, having suffered a heavy 6-1 defeat away to Magdeburg immediately after an impressive 4-0 home victory against Darmstadt. However, goals from Tim Civeja and Marvin Wanitzek secured a deserved victory over the recently-relegated side last weekend, with Wanitzek's superb free-kick proving decisive. Despite that result, consistency remains a significant concern for Senft. Karlsruhe have collected 11 points from their opening ten league matches, leaving them level with Bochum, although their inferior goal difference places them two positions below Sunday's opponents. Their away form is another area requiring improvement, with the visitors yet to record an away victory in the league this season, collecting just two points from their four matches on the road. Senft acknowledged that his team must become more consistent when discussing their recent performances, explaining that the squad are still developing under his new tactical approach. item.title: Max Eberl would love to bring £50m player to Bayern Munich
item.description: Max Eberl would love to bring £50m player to Bayern Munich Bayern Munich are expected to sign a new winger, either in the January window or next summer, and several names have been linked with a move already. One of the players who is of interest to Bayern is Antonio Nusa, who has impressed heavily at RB Leipzig in the past 15 months. Bayern were heavily linked with a move for JJ Gabriel of Manchester United , but the youngster has decided to join Real Madrid instead. Bayern Munich interested in Antonio Nusa? View this post on Instagram Christian Falk has exclusively told CFBayern Insider that Bayern had shown interest in Nusa during the summer window. Max Eberl really likes the player and would love to bring him to Bayern. The Bavarian giants are looking for a back-up for Luis Diaz in the left-wing role, but Nusa would provide direct competition to the Colombian. Falk said: “ It is TRUE: Antonio Nusa was on Bayern’s radar in the summer.Max Eberl loves this player and would really like to bring him to Bayern Munich. As I mentioned, Bayern were looking for a potential backup option to Luis Diaz, but Nusa is no “backup”. He wants frequent game time in the starting XI. Also, it’s worth noting that RB Leipzig paid €21m [£17.5m] for the Norway international; great business it has to be said. However, if Bayern Munich are at the table, €21m will not be enough. I heard that there were talks in the range of €50m-60m [£41.6m-50m]. “This would have been too much for a backup signing. So, I don’t think there’s a chance to bring Nusa to Munich next summer but in the end you have to see what happens with the other players. We’ve mentioned players who are two or three years younger and can develop. But if it doesn’t work out, like with JJ Gabriel, perhaps Nusa can come up in conversation again. Of course, negotiations between RB Leipzig are Bayern Munich typically difficult and expensive! So, I’m not sure if it will work. “ Antonio Nusa would be a fantastic signing (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) The 21-year-old joined RB Leipzig in the summer of 2024, and has made 85 appearances for the club, scoring 16 goals across all competitions. Usually, he plays on the left, but can also play on the right and through the middle, and his versatility could be an asset for Vincent Kompany. Nusa has a contract at Leipzig until 2029, and Falk has suggested that it will not be easy for Bayern to negotiate deals in their favour with their Bundesliga rivals.

item.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga set for emotional Athletic Club homecoming at San Mames as Arsenal backup goalkeeper is called up by Basque Country to face Venezuela
item.description: Girona FC v Arsenal FC - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque Country representative team. The shot-stopper has been named in the Euskal Selekzioa squad to take on South American visitors Venezuela during next weekend's international friendly in Bilbao. Record-breaking keeper returns to Bilbao Osasuna manager Jagoba Arrasate has included the Ondarroa native as one of the marquee names in his 22-man selection for the clash on Saturday, November 14. Currently serving as understudy to David Raya at Arsenal following previous loan stints with Real Madrid and Bournemouth, Arrizabalaga originally departed Bilbao for Chelsea in 2018. That €80 million move to Stamford Bridge remains the world-record transfer fee ever paid for a goalkeeper. Foreign-based trio join domestic core Joining Arrizabalaga in the squad as players plying their trade outside Spain are Udinese forward Unai Gomez and Bolton Wanderers attacker Gaizka Larrazabal, while Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez provides competition between the posts. Arrasate has once again leaned heavily on a familiar domestic core drawn from Athletic Club, Real Sociedad, Osasuna and Deportivo Alaves. In defence, Athletic's Dani Vivian, Hugo Rincon and Johaneko Louis-Jean are joined by Sociedad trio Jon Pacheco, Igor Zubeldia and Aihen Munoz alongside Osasuna's Inigo Arguibide and Malaga's Einar Galilea. Midfield options feature Athletic's Mikel Jauregizar, Sociedad's Benat Turrientes, Alaves pair Pablo Ibanez and Ander Guevara, Osasuna's Asier Osambela and Sevilla's Jon Guridi, while Athletic star Oihan Sancet, Osasuna's Kike Barja and Racing Santander duo Inigo Vicente and Asier Villalibre complete the attack. Historic friendly honours cultural ties Organised by Basque Football Federation president Xabier Goni, the fixture marks the representative team's first appearance since defeating Palestine 3-0 in front of a record 51,396 crowd on November 15 last year via goals from Unai Elgezabal, Gorka Guruzeta and Urko Izeta. Next Saturday's contest carries deep cultural weight as it celebrates the 90th anniversary of the first autonomous Basque Government formed under President Jose Antonio Aguirre in 1936. Aguirre subsequently established the Euzkadi team in 1937 to tour Europe and the Americas during the Spanish Civil War. Venezuela also holds a special bond with the region after welcoming thousands of Basque political exiles fleeing Francisco Franco's dictatorship. Hosts defend flawless head-to-head record Arrrizabalaga will hope to earn rare starting minutes in familiar surroundings next weekend before returning to north London to resume his backup duties under Mikel Arteta after the international break. item.title: Packers Get Discouraging Trade Message On Colts’ Jonathan Taylor
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts scores a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have been among the teams interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment suggests a blockbuster deal is unlikely, even with the NFL trade deadline approaching. Green Bay’s rushing offense has struggled through eight games, yet one Packers beat writer believes the reasons go beyond who is carrying the football. And the Packers’ draft-pick situation presents another obstacle. Packers Get Discouraging Jonathan Taylor Trade Assessment The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman cast doubt on Green Bay acquiring Taylor or two other running backs mentioned as trade candidates. “I don’t see the Packers trading for a Jonathan Taylor, Breece Hall or Tony Pollard,” Schneidman wrote. The biggest issue isn’t necessarily Taylor’s talent. Schneidman argued that “the run game’s biggest problem is the blocking,” making an expensive backfield addition a questionable fix. Taylor, a former Wisconsin star and three-time Pro Bowler, might also cost a first-round pick. Green Bay already sent its 2027 first-round selection to Dallas as part of the Micah Parsons trade last year. Even if the Colts lower their demands, Schneidman questioned whether the Packers would part with two middle-round selections. He also didn’t see an obvious Green Bay player who would entice another team in a trade package. Then there’s Josh Jacobs. The veteran returned in October after spending six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and remains under an NFL investigation involving additional allegations. Jacobs said Wednesday that he isn’t concerned about missing more games. Schneidman acknowledged a longer absence for Jacobs could change the Packers’ thinking. Otherwise, acquiring Taylor would create another question: Would Green Bay keep both backs, or try to move Jacobs? He also expressed doubts about the logic of pursuing Pollard, who is at a similar career stage to Jacobs. Taylor and Hall could represent longer-term options, but fitting either alongside Jacobs would be difficult. Packers Have Reportedly Checked In on Colts’ Jonathan Taylor The assessment contrasts with reports that Green Bay is interested in acquiring Taylor. NFL.com’s Bobby Kownack reported that the Packers were among teams showing interest, citing NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter. NFL insider Jordan Schultz also previously named Green Bay among interested teams, along with Minnesota, Denver, Cincinnati and the New York Giants . He said the asking price was considered too high, although a trade remained possible. Indianapolis has already traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco.
