item.title: Aleksandar Pavlović wants to win everything with Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Stefan Matzke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not interested in setting modest targets for Bayern Munich this season. The young midfielder has made it clear that the expectations inside the dressing room are as high as ever, with the club aiming to co mpete for every major trophy available. Asked about Bayern’s objectives for the campaign, Pavlović delivered a straightforward answer that should sound familiar to anyone who understands the expectations at the Allianz Arena “We want to win everything: the Champions League, the DFB-Pokal and the Bundesliga title,” Pavlović told Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). There is no shortage of ambition in those words, but Bayern Munich has the squad and quality to make those aspirations realistic. The Bundesliga remains the club’s domestic priority, and Vincent Kom pany will expect his team to maintain its consistency over the course of a demanding league campaign. Bayern also has unfinished business in the DFB-Pokal, a competition they have not won since 2020. Ending that drought would be another important milestone for this group. Then there is the Champions League, the ultimate measuring stick for any Bayern Munich side. Winning the competition re quires more than individual brilliance. It demands consistency, resilience, tactical discipline, and the ability to deliver when the pres sure is at its highest. For Pavlović, these are not simply lofty aspirations. They are the standards expected at Bayern Munic h. The midfielder has grown into an increasingly important part of the squad, and his mentality reflects the club’s ambitions. Wi nning one trophy would represent a successful season for many clubs. At Bayern, the expectation is to chase all th ree. Pavlović clearly understands that distinction. Now the hard part begins: turning those words into silverware. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid
item.description: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid Real Madrid are set to take on Valencia at Mestalla later today as they look to continue their excellent form ahead of the international break. The last seven games have been a breeze for Los Blancos , with Jose Mourinho’s side putting in excellent performances. This has been crucial in strengthening belief in the project that the Portuguese manager is building at the Santiago Bernabeu . Mourinho’s men will be looking to make it eight in a row before the November international break. Standing in their way is Javier Aguirre, an experienced manager who has taken over in an attempt to save Valencia’s sinking ship. Aguirre’s struggles against Real Madrid According to Diario AS , the Mexican manager has faced Los Blancos 27 times in his career, securing just four victories. He has suffered 16 defeats and managed seven draws, giving him a win percentage of just 14.8%. Javier Aguirre has a lot of experience managing on the touchline. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) Interestingly, two of his four victories came during his time as Osasuna manager. The first came in February 2003, when he secured a 1-0 victory over Madrid. Vicente del Bosque was Los Blancos ‘ manager at the time. Aguirre followed that up with a 3-0 victory over Madrid in April 2004. His third triumph came in April 2011, when Real Zaragoza secured a stunning 3-2 victory over Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid at the Bernabeu . His most recent victory came in 2023, when Mallorca defeated Carlo Ancelotti’s side 1-0. Can Aguirre trouble Mourinho again? Aguirre is an experienced manager who knows every trick in the book, and he can make life very uncomfortable for Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid. The Mexican is already said to be preparing with a back five ahead of the game in an attempt to stop Los Blancos ‘ attack. Mourinho will hope to make it eight defeats in a row against Valencia. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre has got the better of Mourinho on occasion, but the two sides could hardly be in more contrasting positions heading into this encounter. Real Madrid are the most in-form team in Europe, while Valencia sit 19th, battling relegation and desperately hoping for a turnaround. Los Blancos are playing their fourth consecutive away match and will hope to emerge victorious against Los Che . It promises to be an exciting battle between two experienced managers, and it remains to be seen whether Mourinho can add another defeat to Aguirre’s poor record tonight.

item.title: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid Barcelona could also turn to Gavi for Sunday’s LaLiga meeting with Atletico Madrid, although Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong remain stronger candidates to replace the injured Rodri, reports Mundo Deportivo For now, manager Hansi Flick has several midfield alternatives available for this clash, with the decision likely to depend on multiple factors, including experience and form. This situation arrives as Rodri has been ruled out after medical tests confirmed a minor injury to his right hamstring. Barcelona announced on November 4 that the midfielder would miss the crucial La Liga fixture, leaving Flick with an important selection decision ahead of the trip to the Metropolitano. Gavi’s inclusion in the discussion is particularly interesting given his experience in high-pressure matches and his ability to adapt to different midfield roles. However, it is crucial to note that the 22-year-old should not be considered the leading candidate at this stage. Bernal and De Jong lead Barcelona’s midfield options Marc Bernal has solid grounds to replace Rodri. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported before, though, Bernal is the most natural replacement for Rodri . The academy graduate has already demonstrated his suitability for the role, having started against Elche, Athletic Club, Rayo Vallecano and Paris Saint-Germain this season. Furthermore, De Jong is another possibility after recovering from his injury problems. The Dutchman returned during the Clasico and subsequently started against Alaves, although he was a substitute against Aston Villa. His experience and ability to control possession offer Flick a different profile from Bernal. Gavi’s experience in decisive matches gives Flick a strong option Gavi’s case is built on his performances during the closing stages of Barcelona’s previous campaign. After recovering from his serious knee injury, the midfielder became an important option for Flick in several demanding fixtures, demonstrating that he could be trusted when the stakes were high. Gavi will bring a different profile than Frenkie de Jong and Bernal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He featured in the Catalan derby against Espanyol, where he operated as a left winger, before starting in tricky away encounters against Osasuna and Getafe. He also played as a central midfielder in El Clasico against Real Madrid, the match in which Barcelona mathematically secured the La Liga title. Those appearances showed Gavi’s tactical flexibility and competitive intensity. His ability to press aggressively, recover possession, and support attacking transitions gives Flick a different midfield profile from both Bernal and De Jong. As stated before, the decision will depend on the type of performance Flick expects against Atletico. Bernal offers the most natural replacement for Rodri, while De Jong brings greater experience in controlling possession. Gav

item.title: Nico Paz: Como director spills the beans on Man United target’s future amid Real Madrid speculation
item.description: Nico Paz: Como director spills the beans on Man United target’s future amid Real Madrid speculation Manchester United are laying down succession plans for their mercurial skipper Bruno Fernandes . The Portuguese’s spectacular 2025/26 campaign, during which he registered a record 21 assists in the Premier League, helped the Red Devils finish third in the league. If supporters expected the 32-year-old to continue his golden run this campaign, they have been left disappointed. Fernandes has managed five goals and just two assists in 13 games across all competitions to date, and United are subsequently 17th in the league table after nine games. It is clear that the English giants are heavily reliant on their talisman, and every time he struggles, the team hits an off note as well. With Fernandes also in the final 12 months of his contract, it is imperative that United bring in an able heir soon. Recent reports suggest that they have found a candidate in Como starlet Nico Paz . United want Nico Paz Paz has been a revelation since leaving Real Madrid to join Como in the summer of 2024. Last season, the 22-year-old registered 13 goals and eight assists in 40 games across all competitions. This campaign, the Argentine has hit a higher gear, and has already amassed six goals and eight assists in 13 appearances. United got a first-hand account of the player’s capabilities when he single-handedly destroyed them in the Champions League last week. Paz scored two goals and set up one more as Cesc Fabregas’ side secured a 4-1 win at home. The Argentine’s performance has reportedly convinced the Red Devils, but Los Blancos are looming large amid speculation of a buy-back clause. Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi has now provided an update on the player’s future. N. Paz Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 Paz 100% a Como player Speaking to Radio Radio, as cited by Tuttomercatoweb , Ludi insisted that he feels sorry for Como fans because they have to deal with transfer rumours every year. He said: “I put myself in the shoes of Como’s supporters, because every November and every March – whether due to media speculation or for other reasons – it always comes up that Real Madrid are taking all their players back home.” “This year the talk is of Jacobo Ramon and, over the next two seasons, of Nico Paz.” The Italian club’s sporting director acknowledged Los Blancos’ buy-back clause in Paz’s deal, but hinted that any potential sale would be on Como’s terms. He continued: “The truth is that we struck a good deal last summer. Nico Paz is 100 per cent a Como player. Real Madrid have retained a buy-back option until a specific date during the transfer window, as is to be expected.” “It would, however, be a sale that would recognise the value of our work and would also be important for the club. We’ll work out how to manage the situation during the season, as we’ve always done over the years, thanks in part to the fantastic relationship we have with Madrid.” “For now, we must enjoy ha

item.title: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break
item.description: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break Schalke will hope to end their abysmal run before the international break as they face fellow strugglers Hoffenheim away from home. Hoffenheim After three away games in a week, Christian Ilzer's men will be back at SNP Arena on Sunday night. The Sinsheim side failed to win those fixtures in three different competitions. The defeat in Bremen ended a two-game winning streak in Bundesliga, days after they were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by 2. Bundesliga outfit Holstein Kiel. And, on Thursday, they were very close to upset Europa Conference League winners Crystal Palace before an injury-time strike by former Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Daichi Kamada undone them. However, Hoffenheim won their last two home games 3-0 against Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen. Team News Adam Hložek and Vladimir Coufal weren't in the traveling squad in London, but they both could make their return on Sunday. Alexander Prass, who scored Hoffenheim's goal against Palace, will be back after missing last week's defeat to Bremen due to suspension. Schalke Since the return of club football from October's international break, Schalke 04 have only picked up a single point in the Bundesliga. Miron Muslić’s men were also knocked out of the cup by 2. Bundesliga club Dynamo Dresden as they only scored one goal in their last six competitive games. On matchday 8, Schalke’s search for a first home goal was unsuccessful as they were dominated from start to finish by RB Leipzig, who lost all their previous away matches until that point. Schalke’s next two games at Veltins Arena will also be against Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund. Team News Soufiane El-Faouzi and Robin Gosens returned to training weeks after their head collision in the goalless draw with Köln. As it usually happens with out-of-form clubs, Muslić will be expected to once again make multiple changes to his starting lineup. Head-to-head Hoffenheim were victorious in each of the last four meetings with Schalke, who returned to top-flight football this term. Klaas-Jan Huntelaar, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting and Leroy Sane were on target when the Royal Blues last won at Hoffenheim nearly a decade ago. Predicted Lineups Click here to see our predicted Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 lineups.

item.title: How will Barcelona line up against Atlético Madrid?
item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images | Getty Images Barcelona look to go into the final international break of the season with a statement win in the bag as the La Liga leaders travel to the capital for a monster top of the table clash against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano . Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Sunday’s battle: Defense Barça are expecting to have an almost fully healthy and fit squad after the break if there are no issues during the international window, and they will also have Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen in the squad for Sunday. But the two defenders have not trained long enough to be ready to start, so we expect the same back four in front of Joan Garcia that kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa: Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín at center-back, João Cancelo at left-back, and Brian Fariñas , who continues to impress since getting his first opportunity last weekend, starting at right-back. Midfield Barça will be without Rodri with a minor hamstring issue and there’s a real doubt about who will Flick choose to partner Pedri and Fermín López . Marc Bernal had a strong substitute cameo as Rodri’s replacement in midweek and has been Flick’s first backup choice to the Spain captain so far this season, but Frenkie de Jong is back to 100% and ready to step back into his favorite midfield role. We think Flick will go with the Dutchman for this one, which will likely cause a slight change of formation with a double pivot of Frenkie and Pedri and Fermín as the number 10. Attack Lamine Yamal and Raphinha shined against Villa and will be looking for another big night against Atlético’s tough defense, and we think Flick will once again trust Anthony Gordon ahead of Karim Adeyemi for this one. Possible XI : Joan; Fariñas, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; De Jong, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha (4-2-3-1) How do you think Barcelona should line up against Atlético Madrid? Let us know your thoughts, predictions and teams in the comments below!

item.title: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms
item.description: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms The link between local music and Manchester City fans has always been present, most obviously through Britpop legends Oasis, and now a new kit release has brought a different Greater Manchester artist to the doorstep. Stockport indie outfit Blossoms, who are also lifelong supporters of the club, have teamed up with the Blues to release a limited run of charity shirts celebrating four decades of local outreach across the region. With City in the Community celebrating its 40th anniversary during the ongoing 2026/27 season, main club sponsor Etihad Airways has stepped aside from their front-of-shirt position to make way for the band's logo on the hugely popular 2024/25 away kit. As announced on the club’s official website this week, the special charity drop puts a new spin on a modern favourite. While Blossoms take over the main shirt sponsor space across the chest, the Etihad Airways logo shifts onto the sleeve, sitting alongside a dedicated CITC logo printed inside the neck to mark the anniversary. Blossoms celebrated their fifth Official UK Number One album with 'Songs From The Wedding Cake' last month and are about to head out on a major arena tour across the country. Anyone hoping to pick up a shirt will have to act fast, with initial sizes dropping exclusively at the new flagship CityStore before further batches go on sale around their upcoming homecoming shows at Manchester's Co-op Live in November and December. Four decades of supporting Greater Manchester Founded back in 1986, City in the Community has spent 40 years delivering health, education, and social inclusion initiatives to youth across Greater Manchester, and all profits from the special shirt drop will go straight to the charity to help sustain its daily programmes and expand its reach throughout the local area. To make an even bigger impact across the campaign, Manchester City will match every fan donation made to the foundation on a pound-for-pound basis until the end of May, up to a total of £200,000. As Enzo Maresca's side keep pushing for results on the pitch, this joint effort between local musicians, sponsors, and Manchester City gives fans another brilliant reason to get behind the community off it. On the pitch, Enzo Maresca and his players will be wanting to maintain the winning performance they showed in the UEFA Champions League and a 2-3 victory at RB Leipzig , and taking those levels into their next Premier League clash away to Nottingham Forest .

item.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
item.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”

item.title: How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Passengers inside a commercial bus, popularly called Danfo in Lagos were stunned when a fellow passenger suddenly went into sudden labor and successfully gave birth to a baby boy on board. According to Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the woman was traveling across the state when labor began unexpectedly mid-journey In the process, fellow commuters and onlookers quickly assisted her through the delivery inside the vehicle while others went into prayer session for safe delivery. Medical responders and local commuters assisted in securing the mother and child immediately following the emergency delivery. Fortunately, after few minutes, the baby boy was delivered safely. In viral footage capturing the moments following the birth, witnesses suggested naming the child Abiona—a traditional Yoruba name commonly associated with a child born on a journey or along the road. Recall that a similar incident happened at Onipanu Bus Stop, along Ikorodu Road sometimes ago. “In a swift r​esponse, LASEMA arrived at the scene to assist a pregnant woman who went into sudden labor while waiting for transport. “The woman delivered a healthy baby boy. Both mother and child were stabilized by LASEMA paramedics before being transported to a nearby healthcare facility for post-natal care,” LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu stated. The post How pregnant woman delivered inside Danfo in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Records Are On The Ballot
item.description: The campaign has acquired a sharper edge: In Akwa Ibom Today, President Bola Tinubu challenged the leadership credentials of his principal opponents. His apparent references to Peter Obi’s handling of erosion in Anambra and Atiku Abubakar’s departure from the PDP sought to turn their past decisions into questions about their fitness to govern. These were campaign accusations, rather than independently established assessments of their records. Vice-President Kashim Shettima reinforced the attack, questioning Obi’s credibility and arguing that Atiku’s experience should be judged by accomplishments rather than years in office. His assertion that Obi has lost goodwill remains a partisan assessment; it does not establish a measurable change in voter support. The political intention is clear: put the challengers on the defensive. That matters for an incumbent whose own performance is under examination. If voters spend more time debating whether the opposition is credible, the government gains room to argue that continuity is the safer choice. But scrutiny travels both ways. Once the campaign becomes a comparison of records, Tinubu must also answer for the results of his presidency: purchasing power, security, employment and public services. UYO: Projects and Political Persuasion Today’s visit combined the inauguration of projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration with a political gathering. It gave Tinubu a setting in which visible infrastructure and electoral advocacy could reinforce each other. The distinction between state projects and federal achievements still matters. Political cooperation can support delivery, but credit should follow the evidence about funding, execution and responsibility. For the governing camp, the opportunity is to connect infrastructure with an argument about competent government. For voters, the question is how those investments improve transport, commerce, services and livelihoods. An inauguration provides a powerful picture. Its electoral value depends on the public’s experience after the ceremony. ATIKU: Defiance Needs a Legal Foundation Atiku’s response today remained combative. In a statement, he accused the government of using the courts to evade electoral judgment and reaffirmed his intention to challenge the ruling. That allegation requires attribution; it is not proof of government direction of the proceedings. His campaign also continued in Kebbi on Thursday, despite the judgment. Reporting published today describes promises on security, employment and restoring fuel subsidies. The event should therefore be treated as yesterday’s campaign activity, rather than a fresh Friday rally. Politically, continuing to campaign signals resolve. Legally, public assurances cannot settle the status of a nomination. The subsidy proposal also deserves close questioning. What would be subsidised? Who would benefit? item.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
item.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 7 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. De Gerlache-Kocher Massif Explanation: De Gerlache-Kocher massif looms on the visible horizon in this close-up of the edge of the Moon. The mountainous formation rises about 4 kilometers above its surroundings and is located very close to the lunar south pole. Boasting permanently shadowed crater floors that likely contain deposits of water ice and peaks that receive almost continuous sunlight for solar power generation, the south polar region is consider a prime location for the first human settlement on the Moon. In fact , De Gerlache-Kocher massif itself has been consider as a potential landing site for future crewed Artemis missions to the Moon . The remarkable telescopic image of the massif at the lunar limb was captured on October 31. Then, a favorable libration angle or lunar wobble enhanced this oblique view across the Moon’s south pole. item.title: 2027: Opposition’s battle for space
item.description: Within a span of one week, opposition political parties in Nigeria have experienced various challenges in their bid to contest in the 2027 general elections. From the bids for the presidency to governorship, national assembly and state assembly seats, opposition candidates have not been finding it easy to campaign as they wish as they are faced with various forms of harassment, suppression and intimidation. Weekend Trust reports that 31 states in the country are under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) while two of the remaining five opposition governors have been included in the presidential campaign council of the party. Our correspondents recall that within the week, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was attacked in Cross Rivers State, while the bid by the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to hold a rally in Sokoto met with stiff opposition and in Edo and Plateau States, the billboards of major opposition candidates were pulled down. Habiba: The woman behind ‘Jaiz Bank’s N100m investment scheme’ The night of January 15, 1966 – General Paul Tarfa On Thursday, a Federal High Court sitting in Abuja also nullified all the processes of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) that led to the emergence of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgement, nullified the emergence of the former Senate President, David Mark, Rauf Aregbesola and others as national officers of the ADC. The judge held that the nominations of candidates for the 2027 general elections were cancelled on account of emerging from an “illegal and unlawful leadership.” In the same day, the presidential campaign convoy of the ADC was reportedly attacked in Kebbi State, as the candidate, Atiku, moved through Kebbi on campaign engagements on Thursday. According to reports from the campaign team, thugs blocked the convoy and pelted vehicles with stones. These developments, according to political observers, represent a systematic weakening of opposition parties and raise concerns over Nigeria’s democracy. Due to the frequency in occurrence, opposition figures and civil society organisations have accused the ruling party, APC, of utilizing state-backed coercion, judicial manipulation, and targeted inducements to systematically dismantle counter-balancing political structures across the country. Critics warn that by neutralising alternative political platforms ahead of upcoming electoral cycles, the APC-led administration is actively eroding the essential checks and balances required for democratic accountability. Efforts to get the ruling party (APC) at the national level to respond to the allegations proved abortive as the National Publicity Secretary of the party, Felix Morka, did not respond to phone calls or WhatsApp messages sent to him. However, in a press statement issued Friday, Morka dismissed allegations by the ADC, which accused the ruling party of coll

item.title: Habiba: The woman behind ‘Jaiz Bank’s N100m investment scheme’
item.description: The protest over the N104 million Mudarabah investment and the alleged withdrawal from customers’ accounts at Jaiz Bank, Jos, on Monday, has raised questions with many asking how such could have occurred. One staff member of the bank, Habiba Abdulrahman, is at the centre of the scandal. Mrs Abdulrahman, 35, is a resident of Muhammadu Wada Street, Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. She had her primary education at Women Association Primary School, Jos. Thereafter, she proceeded to Federal Government Girls’ College, Bauchi. In 2009, she gained admission into the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University (ATBU), Bauchi, where she read Environmental Management Technology. She taught at Esteem Secondary School. And between 2018 and 2019, she was employed by Jaiz Bank as a contract customer service officer and subsequently rose to the position of Operations Head (Backup), with the primary duty of approving withdrawals and transfers initiated by tellers in the bank. 2027: Opposition’s battle for space The night of January 15, 1966 – General Paul Tarfa Weekend Trust gathered that Habiba was sacked by the bank in January 2026, after the irregularities were detected. On Monday this week, affected customers who found their accounts emptied by the alleged sacked staff staged a protest in front of the bank in Jos, asking it to refund their money. They also called on the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and other relevant authorities to come to their aid, adding that despite several complaints to the bank’s management, the money had not been refunded. The customers alleged that when the matter was earlier reported to the bank’s management, they were informed that the money had been transferred to several bank accounts by a staff member. The protesters insisted that the transactions were carried out within the banking hall using documents approved by the bank. The protesters at the entrance of the bank on Monday. We found fake Jaiz Bank certificates of fixed deposits, documents in Habiba’s house – Police Following a complaint to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the Plateau State police command by the Jaiz Bank Jos branch manager, Victoria Amidu, in January this year, the CID arrested Habiba, Weekend Trust gathered. In its findings dated June 19, 2026, obtained by Weekend Trust from the lawyer of one of the victims, N. A. Idoko, the CID accused Habiba of conspiracy, cheating and fraud during her transactions with the affected customers. The police also accused Habiba of conniving with her husband, Manir Murtala, 44, and her younger sister, Zainab Abdulrahman, 21, whose accounts were allegedly used to transfer customers’ money into theirs. According to the report, after a search warrant was conducted in the house and premises of the suspects, some relevant Jaiz Bank documents were recovered from her possession. item.title: The night of January 15, 1966 – General Paul Tarfa
item.description: General Paul Chabiri Tarfa joined the Nigerian Army as a cadet in 1962 and remained there until 1988, serving for 26 years. In that span of time he held many positions – Assistant Adjutant General, Provost Marshal, Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy. He also served as the governor of the old Oyo State in 1978. After retirement, he served as the managing director of the Nigerian Railways and also had a brief assignment to reorganise the Nigerian Customs. At 85, he is still busy as the chairman of the North-East Development Commission. He shared his experiences with Weekend Trust. I would like to start with your home, Garkida, which I think is a well-known centre for missionary and western education. Do you think the fact that you were born there has had a very huge impact on how your life turned out? Of course, Garkida is one of the old places in the North where missionaries set up and gave us good footing in education. I must say that in those days we were privileged to have been among the early people in the North, especially the North-East, to be introduced to western education. Habiba: The woman behind ‘Jaiz Bank’s N100m investment scheme’ 2027: Opposition’s battle for space That is not to say that Islamic education was not there, but surely, we were lucky to have the missionaries as far back as March 1923, to be precise. You can imagine that it is well over 100 years now. We have benefitted. We had early education and were introduced to secondary school. We had good medical care, which many of our people in the North were not privileged to have. We went from primary to secondary school, from where we had the advantage of being successfully qualified to get enrolled into the Nigerian Army. I think you went to secondary school in Yola and not Garkida, right? Well, Garkida laid the foundation before going to Yola – provincial secondary school in those days. There were only 12 in the entire North and Yola was one of them. It was from there that I had the opportunity to get into the army. You became a cadet in the army in April 1962, but it didn’t take long before you were taken to Canada, a very strange place for someone coming from this part of the world. Before going there, we were told what it would be. Even before then, in Geography in secondary school, we had known about temperate countries, hot countries and so on, of which Canada was one. So when we got to Canada, we were very well equipped and properly prepared, physically and mentally. Your career in the army took off after you returned to Canada. This was 1963? Yes. We came back in December 1963, received at Kano airport, taken to Kaduna and received by the duty officer, who at that time happened to be a man called Benjamin Adekunle. He was a captain and we were just second lieutenants. The so-called “black scorpion”? He asked: “Who among you is Paul Tarfa?” I said I was the one and he said “congratulations”. item.title: Anambra will deliver over 50% of 2027 votes to Tinubu — Soludo
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has promised to deliver at least 50 percent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu, the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the 2027 general elections. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ The governor made the declaration during the flag off of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) 2027 campaign at Ekwueme Square, Awka. According to him, APGA has no presidential candidate for the 2027 general election and would, therefore, adopt President Tinubu as its preferred candidate. “Today, we adopt the APC presidential candidate, Bola Ahmed Tinubu as our candidate,” he declared, noting that the president had demonstrated love and concern for the Igbo people, particularly the people of Anambra State. The governor recalled that the President had appointed several Anambra indigenes to strategic positions in Lagos State during his tenure as governor. He also recalled that APGA had adopted the presidential candidate of the ruling party in previous elections, noting that the party’s decision to support Tinubu in 2027 was a continuation of that political arrangement that had been in existence. He lamented that Anambra State recorded fewer than 5,000 votes for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, yet the President has continued to address some of the challenges confronting the state and the South-East region. He urged the Anambra electorate to support Tinubu in the 2027 election, arguing that doing so would give the state and the South-East a stronger opportunity to engage with the Federal Government and negotiate for their development. “We need to vote for him in order to sit with the government at the centre and negotiate for the development of the South-East and Anambra State”, he declared. item.title: Tinubu’s reforms need time to deliver, 2nd term will consolidate gains — Aguda
item.description: Oluwole Aguda is a businessman, consultant on electoral mat- ters and political affairs, and a former governorship aspirant in Kogi State, under the African Action Con- gress (AAC) in 2019. In this interview, he examines President Bola Tinubu’s reform agenda, the steps the President must take to secure electoral support in the North ahead of the 2027 general election, and the political implications of the lingering face-off between Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and his predecessor, Senator Rochas Okoro- cha, over the Imo West senatorial ticket. Excerpts: Given the hardship caused by fuel subsidy removal, naira devaluation and other economic policies, what tangible improvements in Nigerians’ living conditions can President Tinubu point to as justification for seeking a second term? A fair assessment requires us to examine the immediate challenges confronting the economy and the long-term benefits expected from the reforms. Nigeria’s economy was bleeding, and stopping that haemorrhage was necessary to give the country a chance of recovery. Ending fuel subsidy addressed an avenue for corruption and the unsustainable drain on public resources. NELFUND had disbursed over N300 billion to over 1.5m students across 319 tertiary institutions as at October 2026. However, I would not suggest that these developments have largely translated into improved living conditions for most Nigerians. That remains the administration’s biggest challenge. The cost of food, transportation, housing, healthcare and other essentials continues to put enormous pressure on households. Economic recovery must ultimately be measured by whether people can afford necessities, businesses can employ more workers and incomes can support a reasonable standard of living. The President’s case for another term should not rest solely on the courage to introduce reforms. It must also depend on translating them into better purchasing power, employment, productivity and social welfare. Reforms require time, but Nigerians enduring difficult adjustments must see a credible pathway to relief. How would you assess the Tinubu administration’s performance, and what justifies giving it another four years? There is intention coupled with execution across different sectoral interventions. While execution has been a challenge, progressive steps have been made. Investment in our military is important to sustaining a motivated Army, Navy and Air Force in the war against terrorism. The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway also promises to reduce travel time and transportation costs between the South-West and South-South. One foundational challenge to national growth has been the lack of continuity in government policies, including those that could have delivered long-term benefits if sustained. Policy reversals have been the bane of our collective development. Any purposeful course must be entrenched long enough for its benefits to have an impact. item.title: US offers $20m reward for info on ‘Iran’s nuclear program’: CENTCOM
item.description: Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. Read Also: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X. The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges. It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward. Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program. “If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.” But the president also said Iran – which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war – is eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said. Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting. And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. item.title: Trump: Lesson for Nigeria, by Stephanie Shaakaa
item.description: Donald Trump wanted the November 3 midterm elections to be about him. He said so repeatedly, urging Americans to vote as though his name were on the ballot. He wanted a Republican victory to demonstrate that his presidency still commanded popular support and that his influence over American politics remained firmly intact. Well, Americans took him seriously. Perhaps more seriously than he expected. Democrats have won control of both chambers of the United States Congress, delivering a major electoral setback to Trump and his Republican Party. Yet, as the results became clear, Trump reached for an explanation that seemed to contradict his own campaign message. In a post on his Truth Social platform, he declared: “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The irony is difficult to miss. He had spent weeks asking Americans to treat the election as a verdict on his presidency. When the verdict went against him, he suddenly appeared to be distancing himself from it. He wanted the political benefits of making the election about him without accepting the consequences when voters delivered an unfavourable answer. For readers in Nigeria, it is worth explaining what America calls midterm elections and why they matter. In the United States, a president is elected for a four-year term, but congressional elections take place every two years. This means that halfway into a president’s tenure, Americans return to the polls to elect members of the legislature. These elections are called midterms because they take place in the middle of a presidential term. Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, while senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the 100 Senate seats contested every two years. Midterm elections do not determine who becomes president. The sitting president remains in office. Instead, voters decide which party controls Congress and, by extension, how much support or opposition the president will face in the legislature This gives Americans an opportunity to express satisfaction or dissatisfaction with a president’s performance without waiting another four years. They can strengthen the president’s party in Congress or hand control to the opposition, making it considerably more difficult for the president to advance his legislative agenda. That is precisely what has happened to Trump. American presidents often benefit from what is known as the coattail effect. When a president is popular, candidates from the same party can benefit from that popularity. His political strength becomes an advantage for others seeking elective office. But when a president becomes unpopular, the effect can work in reverse. Candidates associated with his administration may find themselves paying the price for public dissatisfaction with his leadership. In political terms, this is sometimes described as negative or reverse coattails. Tru

item.title: From open pavilion to nation of orderlies: Is Zik’s ‘fear-free’ Nigeria still possible?
item.description: .What a 1960 inauguration says about fear in today’s corridors of power By Omeiza Ajayi Nearly 66 years after Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was sworn in as Nigeria’s first African Governor-General, the footage of that day – which has again recently gone viral – raises an uncomfortable question: why did a leader who held the highest office in the land need no retinue of security details standing behind him, while today every minister, and even some local government supervisors, cannot move without a swarm of details? The inauguration took place on November 16, 1960, at Tafawa Balewa Square, barely six weeks after independence. It was also Zik’s 56th birthday. The narrator of the newsreel set the scene plainly. “At the steps of the pavilion stand the Prime Minister and the Lord Chief Justice, symbolising the people and the law, on what is surely one of the most important occasions in the history of the country.” No armed escort looms in the frame. No aide hovers at the shoulder of the man the crowd was chanting for. “Zik! Zik!” rang around the square as he arrived, and the vast stands, in the narrator’s words, were “hushed.” Today the picture is reversed. In Abuja and in the state capitals, orderlies trail ministers into halls and offices. The situation is so bad that some security personnel actually enter into very enclosed spaces or rooms with their AK47 rifles in clear breach of security protocol. At the local government level, some unelected supervisory councillors have been known to move with armed vigilance team members or hunters, sometimes to intimidate the very people they were appointed to serve. The easy explanation is insecurity, and it is not a false flag. Banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have made parts of the country dangerous, and no leader can be faulted for fearing for his life. But the leaders of other nations also face threats. Behind the American president or a British prime minister stand trained protective officers, assigned to a defined danger. They do not crowd every public official, from the cabinet room to the ward office, with men whose chief duty is to announce importance. It is not uncommon in Nigeria to see security details standing and blocking a television camera. That leaves the harder question. Are Nigeria’s leaders afraid of the general state of the country, or have they become afraid of their own people? Zik, standing in the open that November morning, appeared to have settled that question for himself. He began his address with these words: “It is with humility, mingled with joy, that I thank this grand concourse of patriots and friends of Nigeria for congregating here today on the occasion of my inauguration as the first African Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of the Federation of Nigeria.” He titled the speech “Respect for Human Dignity,” and he made no secret of what he feared for Nigeria. It was not assassins. It was division. “I appeal to all our leaders, far and near, to forget the wounds which were inflic

item.title: Daddy Showkey: Vanguard Award will be the biggest of my lifetime
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe & Benjamin Njoku Chief John Odafe Asiemo, 57, popularly known as Daddy Showkey, is a household name in Nigerian music scene. He is the creator of ‘Galala’ music, which sound helped define Nigeria’s street music in the 90s. Read Also: Nostalgia, glitz as icons reunite for Daddy Showkey’s 50th anniversary celebration Daddy Showkey is a nominee for Vanguard Newspaper’s 2026 Entertainment Icon of the year award. Speaking with ululation after being presented with the letter of nomination, on Tuesday at his Lagos residence, he said: “They say a prophet is not recognised by his own people. But I am a prophet who is being recognised by the people who built me. This is the greatest awards I have ever received in my life because it is coming from Vanguard. Vanguard is the first newspaper in Nigeria that wrote about me, when I was nothing. This is Vanguard, and I cherish it a lot. “Apart from that, Vanguard played a big role in pushing me to the limelight. “So, a recognition award coming from Vanguard, I must cherish it. It is like my own people saying it is high time. Sometimes, when I see Vanguard giving people awards, I always say in my mind, when is it going to be my turn? “Now, it is my turn to receive the award and I am very grateful.” Reminiscing on his early days, Daddy Showkey, who celebrated 50 years on the stage recently, continued: “For years, I kept coming to Vanguard head office, but I never met the publisher, Uncle Sam, in person. After my secondary education, I hit the streets. From childhood, I had made up my mind to follow music. At 13, in 1983, I started following Danladi Bako of NTA. I was always at his office on Lagos Island. He would give me a voucher to go and eat, and made me comfortable in his office. My first song, “Big Belle”, was released in 1990 in Nawfia, Njikoka, Enugu-Ukwu, Anambra State. I cannot forget the late Amadi Ogbonna(former Vanguard Entertainment Editor). He was one of the earliest journalists to write about me and played a huge role in my career. Before Ogbonnaya wrote about me, we used to walk from Kirikiri to Olodi areas, passing Vanguard. I remember saying one day while walking past Vanguard ‘this newspaper will one day write about me.’ It came to pass when Ogbonnaya wrote about me for the first time. The second was Smart Irewudo, a former Champion Newspaper reporter, now based in the United States. Before I started recording, during the June 12 crisis, I led Ajegunle boys who blocked roads and extorted money from motorists. Smart took my picture and published it in the Daily Champion. In his mind, he thought he had done me a great favour. He didn’t know the police would come after me. Luckily, one of the policemen from Area F showed my picture to Amadi Ogbonna. He recognised me immediately and called me. When I showed up, Ogbonna took me to the police station and told them I wasn’t a bad boy, they should release me and focus on arresting real criminals. item.title: Police rescue 10 stolen children in Abia
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Abia State Police Command has arrested suspects linked to the October 17 attack on Uratta Divisional Police Headquarters, rescued 10 stolen children and recovered 15 firearms and 30 stolen vehicles in a major security crackdown across the state. The Command also disclosed that it arrested 109 suspects, comprising 89 males and 20 females, in connection with 211 criminal cases recorded between September 11, 2026 and November 6, 2026. Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, who disclosed this on Friday while presenting the Command’s operational scorecard, said the arrests followed intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies. On the Uratta police station attack, Afolabi said investigations had led to the arrest of some of the suspected attackers, with one of them allegedly confessing to leading the gang that carried out the assault. He said investigations were ongoing to track down other accomplices and establish the full circumstances surrounding the attack. In a related security operation, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit raided a location at Ubakala, Umuahia South Local Government Area, on October 25, arresting a suspect identified as Osita. The police reportedly recovered two locally fabricated guns, 16 live cartridges and four expended cartridges from the suspect. Another suspect, 30-year-old suspect, was subsequently arrested for allegedly supplying ammunition illegally. Both suspects have been charged to court, according to the CP. On child trafficking, Afolabi said police operatives rescued 10 children during the period under review and reunited them with their families. He specifically disclosed that two suspects, including a 38-year-old , were arrested on October 11 over the alleged stealing of two children, seven-year-old Chiamaka Chikeze and nine-month-old Goodluck Chikeze. The children were reportedly recovered and handed back to their parents, while the suspects were charged to court. The police boss also announced the arrest of a five-man vehicle theft syndicate, aged 43, and 40. A Toyota Corolla with registration number ROU 9338J was recovered from the suspects, who have also been charged to court. In another operation, two suspected cultists, aged 27, and 25, were arrested on October 31 for allegedly dispossessing students of Abia State University, Uturu, of their mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint. A locally fabricated firearm was recovered from them. The CP said one of the suspects had confessed to belonging to the Black Axe Confraternity, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend other members of the gang. item.title: ‘Sort out your internal mess’, APC tells Atiku, ADC after court judgment
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The All Progressives Congress APC has told the Senator David Mark-led faction of the African Democratic Congress ADC to go sort out its internal mess and quit its “senseless rants” after a Federal High Court judgment sacked the faction’s leadership. Read Also: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate? In a statement Friday in Abuja, the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the ruling party had no hand in the case. “To be clear, APC is neither a party nor an interlocutor in the matter. Nothing about the case has anything to do with the APC. And the APC has absolutely no role in the party’s judicial quagmire,” he said. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, sacked the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC. It also nullified all official acts of that leadership, including its primary election processes and outcomes, like the presidential candidacy of former vice president Atiku Abubakar. Morka said the case was brought by ADC national officers against the faction now removed from office, describing the suit as “a notorious case initiated by leaders of ADC against pirate leaders of ADC.” He accused Mark and his associates of taking over the party “to satisfy Atiku Abubakar’s quixotic presidential ambition.” According to him, “it didn’t matter to them that their hostile takeover of that party was in flagrant violation of the rule of law and ADC’s internal democracy, as a court of competent jurisdiction has now declared.” The APC spokesman also accused the ADC of reacting to court decisions according to whether they favour it. “Every time a court decides against the Senator David Mark-led factional African Democratic Congress, they accuse the All Progressives Congress of collusion and deprecate the judiciary. Every time a court decides in their favour, they hail the rule of law and extol the judiciary,” he said. He added that the faction’s attitude showed “no iota of regard for the authority and independence of the judiciary, an indispensable pillar of any democracy.” On Thursday’s ruling, Morka said it “was procured by their own lawlessness and demonstrates the vibrancy of the rule of law and independence of the judiciary in Nigeria.” He said the ADC leaders “take no responsibility or accountability for the self-inflicted injury that the court only judicially certified.” Vanguard News The post ‘Sort out your internal mess’, APC tells Atiku, ADC after court judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe What if the chemical produced in abundance by cancer cells could be turned against the cancers? What if, instead of flooding the entire body with powerful drugs in an attempt to destroy a tumour, scientists could persuade cancer cells to manufacture destructive chemicals from within? That possibility is at the centre of an intriguing scientific breakthrough in Japan, where researchers have developed an experimental technique that exploits carbon monoxide produced by cancer cells to generate cancer-killing compounds inside them. The approach turns an unusual feature of cancer biology into a potential therapeutic advantage. Rather than administering an already manufactured toxic drug that circulates through the body and can damage healthy tissues, the researchers have devised a chemical system that produces an anticancer compound inside targeted cancer cells. In laboratory experiments, the technique successfully generated toxic compounds in several cancer cell lines while leaving a noncancerous cell line without detectable production of the same compound. Although still at an early experimental stage, the findings could open a new direction in cancer treatment, particularly in the long-standing search for ways to destroy malignant cells while sparing healthy tissues from the collateral damage associated with conventional chemotherapy. The research, led by Katsunori Tanaka at the RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute (PRI), Japan, was published in Nature Communications. Cancer treatment has long been complicated by a fundamental problem: drugs powerful enough to destroy malignant cells can also injure normal cells. Chemotherapy, for instance, often affects healthy tissues because many anticancer medicines cannot distinguish perfectly between cancerous and noncancerous cells. The resulting damage can produce debilitating side effects, including nausea, fatigue, hair loss and suppression of the immune system. Scientists have consequently been exploring more selective ways of delivering or generating anticancer agents at the precise location where they are needed. Tanaka and colleagues focused on carbon monoxide, a gas commonly recognised for its toxicity but also naturally produced in small quantities in the human body. Their strategy was to deliver a metal-based catalyst into cells and use the available carbon monoxide as the chemical fuel for a reaction that manufactures an anticancer substance. In principle, the reaction would be activated predominantly in cancer cells, where sufficient carbon monoxide is available, rather than in healthy tissues. The research represents part of a developing scientific field known as therapeutic in vivo synthetic chemistry, which seeks to use chemical reactions inside living organisms to manufacture therapeutic substances where they are needed. Vanguard News The post Scientists turn cancer cells into weapons against tumours appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria is losing $1.6bn yearly to avoidable blindness — Aghaji
item.description: By Prisca Sam-Duru Almost on a daily basis, across Nigeria and much of Africa, millions of people wake up to a world they cannot see clearly. A farmer peeks at his cassava farms for instance, but cannot differentiate the difference between weed and crop. A trader holds her register at arm’s length, guessing at figures she once read at a glance. A child in the back row of a classroom copies from a board that is almost a blur. More often, an old woman needs her grandchild to lead her to the market because the road she walked for over 50 years has become unrecognizable. Those are not statistics. They are the human face of a crisis that Africa has lived with for too long. As Professor Ada Aghaji told a packed hall at the University of Nigeria on October 29, 2026, this is a crisis Africa can no longer afford to ignore. Delivering the institution’s 254th Inaugural Lecture, titled “Let There Be Sight: Building Sustainable Eye Health Systems for All in Africa,” Aghaji, Professor of Ophthalmology and Eye Health Systems, made a simple but very powerful argument: eye health in Africa is not just a medical issue. It is an economic issue. A development issue. A justice issue. And the numbers prove it. According to her, Nigeria loses an estimated $1.6 billion every year in productivity because of vision impairment. Across Africa, the loss is about $9 billion. Globally, it stands at a staggering $410 billion. Behind those figures are livelihoods cut short, schooling interrupted, and families pushed deeper into poverty. Yet, as Aghaji stressed, much of this vision loss can be prevented or treated. A pair of spectacles costing less than a bag of rice. A 15-minute cataract operation. A routine screening at a primary health centre. Why, then, do millions of Africans continue to live with avoidable blindness when the solutions already exist? That was the question at the heart of her lecture. Two Children, Two Worlds Perhaps the most haunting moment of the lecture came not from statistics, but from a story. Aghaji spoke of two children born with congenital rubella syndrome; a condition that can cause cataracts, deafness and other disabilities. One was born in Nigeria. He faced delays, barriers to treatment and rehabilitation, and ended up blind. The other was a Somali refugee child in England. He received timely surgery, spectacles and hearing aids, and with them, a chance to learn, to play, to grow Their medical conditions were similar. Their opportunities were profoundly different. The contrast, Aghaji argued, is the story of Africa’s eye health system in miniature. Medical knowledge alone does not guarantee care. What determines whether a child sees or goes blind is often not the disease, but the system around it: whether there is money to pay, a health worker to detect the problem, a referral that works, a hospital that can be reached. It is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said. item.title: ADC Crisis: What becomes of Atiku, Mark, Gombe if Supreme Court decides party’s fate?
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress (ADC) was meant to be the meeting point of opposition forces determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu in 2027. Instead, the party has become the battleground for a struggle that could undo the coalition it was expected to accommodate. Read Also: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy Barely 24 hours after former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar took his presidential campaign to Sokoto, a Federal High Court judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu threw the party into fresh uncertainty, nullifying the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it, including the process that produced Atiku as presidential candidate. For Mark and his allies, it was a setback at a critical moment. For Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the leadership transition, it was a victory in a battle he had refused to abandon. For Atiku, it was a reminder that the platform on which he hopes to return to Aso Rock may not be entirely within his control. With the Mark faction preparing to appeal, attention is shifting to the appellate courts. Whatever the eventual outcome, the political fortunes of some of the coalition’s most prominent figures are at stake. How it all began The dispute began when former ADC National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, facilitated a leadership transition that brought Mark and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola, into the party as National Chairman and National Secretary respectively. The arrangement offered opposition politicians an existing political structure around which to build a challenge to the APC. But Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman, North, objected, arguing that the party’s constitution provided a succession procedure that was not followed. His challenge produced Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment. The Mark faction, however, insists that the leadership question had already been examined by the court. It points to the July 2, 2026, judgment of Justice Musa Liman in a separate suit instituted by House of Representatives member Leke Abejide. Justice Liman upheld preliminary objections, including lack of jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies. He also made findings favourable to the defendants concerning the leadership transition The Mark camp argues that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot overturn another court’s decision. However, the different plaintiffs and the precise issues and reliefs sought in the two cases make the legal relationship between the judgments a matter requiring highest judicial determination. The Supreme Court had intervened on April 30, setting aside an earlier status quo ante bellum order and directing an expedited hearing at the Federal High Court. It did not decide who was entitled to lead the ADC While Mark’s camp rejects the latest judgment, Gombe has celebrated it as a victory for constitutional governance. “Political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not

item.title: ‘Our fathers have spoken’- Middle Belt youths rally behind Tinubu
item.description: Youths from the Middle Belt have declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, announcing plans to mobilise voters across the region for the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group said it would work with the City Boy Movement, led by Seyi Tinubu, its Director-General, Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, and the APC campaign council to coordinate the mobilisation. The initiative is being championed by aviation entrepreneur and political figure, Isaac Balami, who said the decision followed a meeting between Tinubu and prominent Middle Belt leaders led by elder statesman, General Theophilus Yakubu Danjuma. Balami described the engagement at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, as a turning point for the region, saying younger people were ready to follow the political direction established by their elders. “Our fathers have spoken. They have met the father. We have equally met the son. The movement has begun,” he said. Balami recalled that the same elders had asked him to mobilise support for Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi in the 2023 election. He said a fallout over what he described as abandonment had contributed to the latest political realignment. The founder of the National Rebirth Movement, who also serves as an executive board member and National Director on Special Duty of the City Boy Movement, said the decision to support Tinubu was informed by the region’s representation in the administration. He cited appointments to strategic government positions, efforts to tackle insecurity and the inclusion of Middle Belt representatives in national decision-making. “We have people from our region occupying important positions in this government. For us as young people, representation matters,” Balami said. He said the group would mobilise across the Middle Belt, adding that some youths who supported Obi in 2023 were now prepared to back Tinubu. Balami also identified security, infrastructure, education, employment and economic opportunities as issues requiring sustained government attention. He said the movement aimed to involve young people in political decisions affecting the region rather than limit their participation to election campaigns. The announcement follows Thursday’s meeting between Tinubu and a delegation of Middle Belt and North-Central leaders led by Danjuma. The delegation included Defence Minister Christopher Musa, Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang, Taraba State Governor Agbu Kefas, former House of Representatives Speaker Yakubu Dogara and former Chief of Army Staff General Ishaya Bamaiyi. Dogara said the delegation met Tinubu to express solidarity with his administration and discuss security, development and political engagement ahead of the 2027 elections. The emerging youth mobilisation signals an effort to translate the engagement of regional elders into electoral support for Tinubu in an area where Obi secured considerable backing in 2023. item.title: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’
item.description: •Says, I share your pain, we’re out of dark tunnel •Knocks Atiku, Obi in Uyo, approves Ibom Deep Sea Port •Bus conveying women to welcome President crashes By Egufe Yafugborhi UYO — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu yesterday promised a better future for Nigerians even as he took a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), declaring that they lacked the leadership qualities to govern Nigeria. Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t confront Anambra’s erosion, he lacks leadership traits — Tinubu Tinubu, presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, spoke during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno, insisting that continuity was necessary to sustain development. His visit, however, was overshadowed by a road crash involving an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome him, in which one person was feared dead and several others sustained serious injuries. The accident occurred along Oron Road, Uyo, when the bus, reportedly heading towards the airport, collided with a security Hilux van. Both vehicles were badly damaged. Addressing supporters at the rally, Tinubu described his visit as a homecoming, recalling his professional connection with Akwa Ibom through his early employment with Mobil Oil. “It’s like a homecoming for me. I remember having cut my teeth with Deloitte, the greatest accounting firm in America. I expressed the desire to come home. Mobil Oil recruited me. “Part of the first assignment I was given was to audit the operations of Mobil in Eket. We used to go by boat to Ibono Terminal at that time. Akwa Ibom and I have been united ever since then. Till now, they decided that we are going to keep good company,” he said. The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Card (PVCs), describing it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future. “To you, the youth, do you have your PVC? Show me your hand if you have your PVC. To me, that is your sword. That is the weapon you need to defeat tyranny, to defeat those who deceive, those who don’t appreciate the value of a growing economy and the value of promising prosperity. “The weapon you have is the PVC. I don’t have to enumerate what I’ve done for you. I’ve committed my last years to struggling for democracy, freedom, authenticity, development and progress,” Tinubu said. He urged the people to support continuity, arguing that his administration had delivered improvements in education and other sectors. “Have you seen development or not? You have seen progress. Your university is no longer on strike. There’s economic value being added to your life,” he told the crowd. item.title: CBN updates guidelines for stablecoins operation
item.description: •Sets N15bn capital requirement By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria has issued guidelines for virtual asset providers in the country, setting minimum capital requirement of N10 billion and N15 billion for Classes 1 and 2 issuers, respectively. This was contained in a circular with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, date November 5, 2026 and signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Mr. Musa Jimoh. According to the bank, “A Class 1 Licensed Issuer shall maintain paid-up capital of N10 billion Naira or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. Class 2 Licensed Issuer shall maintain minimum paid-up capital of N15 billion or such higher amount as the Bank may prescribe, on entry and at all times thereafter. “Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital.” Class 2 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against foreign currencies, including the US dollar, while Class 1 refers to issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins. CBN said the emergence of virtual assets, stablecoins, and tokenised payment instruments “presents significant opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlement, and digital commerce,” but that, “their growing adoption also introduces risks relating to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, illicit finance, operational resilience, and foreign exchange management.” It added that the guidelines were issued pursuant to its statutory mandate to promote monetary and financial stability and regulate Nigeria’s payments system. “These Guidelines establish a risk-based framework for the licensing, regulation, supervision, and oversight of Non-Security Virtual Assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs), and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). “These Guidelines seek to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability, and efficiency of the Nigerian financial system. “These Guidelines also seek to provide regulatory requirements relating to governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, AML/CFT/CPF compliance, and reporting obligations for entities and persons engaged in regulated non-security virtual asset activities within or involving Nigeria,” the bank explained. The CBN’s updated framework outlines clear boundaries for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), with a sharp focus on foreign exchange liquidity, consumer protection, and peer-to-peer (P2P) trading identity protocols. Curbing money laundering The guidelines place great responsibilities on issuers to ensure that their activities do not aid money laundering or terrorism financing, as they are required to provide detailed data on their customers.
