item.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (photos)
item.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

item.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
item.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. item.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
item.description: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm , which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile , potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry. Tim Höttges, the CEO of T-Mobile’s parent company Deutsche Telekom, said he takes SpaceX’s plans “super serious” but that it could cost Musk more than $200 billion to pull off. Follow along for the latest updates on Starlink’s major mobile carrier ambitions. What will it take for SpaceX to launch its “major” mobile network? item.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
item.description: Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes. The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times . Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region. Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region's undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
item.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
item.description: null Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today . "This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added. Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites , which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite. BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9 , Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift. The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace , to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly. Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage. Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile. "The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement. The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement. Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. item.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. The protesters called on security agencies and state institutions to intervene and ensure a level playing field for all political parties. Another youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats or intimidation. “Opposition parties must be allowed to campaign safely, present their platforms, and engage with voters without constant threat of violence,” the coordinator said. The group said the march was part of efforts by young people in the state to demand accountability and promote peaceful political participation as the 2027 general elections approach. The post Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
item.description: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register . The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . “And in the first opportunity they saw,” the models shared the secret keys, “similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” The Hugging Face incident - during which a swarm of OpenAI agents built unauthorized message boards to ask other agents for help, exploited zero-day vulnerabilities , gained internet access, stole credentials, and ultimately broke into Hugging Face - inspired this hackathon, de Lucena said. “Given the Hugging Face incident, and everything that's been happening since then, we thought that it made sense to start exploring behaviors that you might get from swarms, what risks are people not seeing yet,” he said. Sandboxed coding test This particular test from the hackathon that saw agents give up their keys to join a forum “is one of the most interesting ones,” according to de Lucena, who explained it has a huge impact on how organizations build IT systems and what access they grant to AI agents. “This was a fairly simple type of instructions - we were not particularly trying to get secretive information from the models,” he told us. “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” Plus, the agents' willingness to run an untrusted script on the host computer “seems like a pretty obvious risk,” he added. “You could get any kind of control over that host if you ran something malicious,” de Lucena said. “The simplicity of making that happen is very surprising. It's not surprising to me that you can get to it, but how little effort you need to put into setting that up to get models to share anything.” The researchers tested nine models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, Z.ai’s GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-5.6-Luna, and GPT-6.1-Sol, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. item.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. item.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
item.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. item.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
item.description: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. item.title: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished between Oakland and Texas
item.description: A shipment of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million vanished in transport between Oakland and Texas over the summer, and more than two months later, police have announced no arrests or recovery of the cargo. As reported by The Mercury News , six pallets of unknown Nvidia equipment left Oakland on August 29 on a truck bound for Fort Worth, Texas. The hardware was reportedly picked up as scheduled by a truck bearing the logo of a food transportation company before vanishing off the grid. The theft wasn't noticed until early September, when the buyers realized that the shipment had never been received. Police attempting to trace the truck's route found it had made several multi-hour stops after picking up the hardware before losing the truck somewhere in San Bernardino County, California. Oakland police confirmed that there was a grand theft report filed on September 13 and that the investigation remains ongoing. Authorities have not said what Nvidia hardware was stolen or exactly how the theft was carried out. Read full article Comments

item.title: I finally got my hands on the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars with augmented reality and I can’t wait to stargaze with them
item.description:
Harry joined Space.com in December 2024 as an e-commerce staff writer covering cameras, optics, and skywatching content. Based in the UK, Harry graduated in 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in American Literature with Creative Writing from the University of East Anglia. A keen photographer, Harry has strong experience with astrophotography and has captured celestial objects with a range of cameras. As a lifelong skywatcher, Harry remembers watching the Perseid meteor shower every summer in his hometown and being amazed by the wonders of the night sky.

I have been waiting to get my hands on a pair of Unistellar Envision smart binoculars since they were announced in 2024. Our editor-in-chief tried an early demo of them last year and said that they felt like something out of Star Trek . He was, of course, referencing the red augmented reality (AR) overlay in the Envisions that can identify night sky targets and landmarks, as well as displaying navigational tools. These are the first pair of smart binoculars that can identify targets in the night sky, such as planets, stars and deep space objects. The build is solid and while they aren't the most lightweight binoculars , the body is hiding that extra technology that enables the AR overlay in the right hand lens. Each pair ships with a soft carry case, a padded neck strap, a USB-C cable and rubber caps for the eyepieces and lenses. The Unistellar Envision smart binoculars are the first ever smart binoculars aimed at night sky observation. Harry Bennett / Future Rubber caps on the lenses keep the glass clean during travel and storage. Harry Bennett / Future The Envisions ship with a soft carry case and a USB-C cable for charging. Harry Bennett / Future (Image credit: Unistellar) Pre-order the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars for $1,499 / £1,299 I would highly recommend setting these binoculars up in the daytime, as you definitely need a few minutes to get used to the controls and to perform the diopter adjustment. After powering on, all I had to do was connect the model to the Unistellar app, which recognised the device easily and then watch the onboarding videos. Unistellar also recommends performing a 360-degree calibration before your first use to help ensure the best performance. You need to have location services set to "always" for the Unistellar app so that it can work out your exact location and give you an accurate reading on the augmented reality (AR) display for locations of night sky targets and landmarks. I haven't had chance to use the night mode on these binoculars yet, thanks to cloudy skies, but I did use the topographical identification and was impressed with the ease of identifying landmarks around my local area. Besides the night and daytime modes, there is also a navigation mode which displays your cardinal direction alongside degrees of your azimuth and elevation angles. item.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
item.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Read more Physics of light and magnetism rewritten after almost two centuries Because the rotor experiences essentially no friction, and it is magnetic and cold, its behaviour is very sensitive to its environment, which makes it a promising sensor. The team has already successfully tested it as a gauge of vacuum at very low temperatures. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Benjamin Stickler at Ulm University in Germany says the levitated spinning magnet could also be used to precisely sense and measure magnetic fields. item.title: An unexpected feedback loop may be driving mega heatwaves
item.description: Land scorched by a fire in Wennington, London, during the record-breaking heatwave in 2022 Shutterstock Mid-latitude regions such as Europe are set to suffer more intense heatwaves than previously thought, according to new research that has uncovered a three-way feedback loop that amplifies extreme heat conditions. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. Advertisement Researchers have been scrambling to understand why very extreme heat is occurring more frequently, and with greater intensity, than expected at this level of warming. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now it seems that when temperatures climb high enough, dry soil, high pressure and extreme heat can amplify each other further, with dry soil helping to sustain high-pressure systems in the atmosphere. “Basically, the soils that are affected by circulation pattern also start to affect back on the circulation pattern itself,” says Kai Kornhuber at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. This will have serious consequences for our ability to cope with future extreme heat. “Ten per cent hotter or colder can really make a difference between a heatwave and a record-shattering heatwave,” says Kornhuber. “We’re facing so many critical thresholds in social and biophysical systems that an extra 10 per cent can really lead to temperatures that are then quite damaging.” Read more Is a broken jet stream causing extreme weather that lasts longer? This may include serious public health consequences, a breakdown of vital infrastructure such as transport links and energy grids, crop failures and the collapse of ecosystems. As the world warms due to climate change, regions including Europe, Russia, North America, parts of South America and Australia will hit thresholds where this feedback effect is triggered increasingly often. item.title: See the space race like you’ve never seen it before in PBS’s new living documentary, ‘We Chose to Go to the Moon’
item.description: null Straight from its inspiring live performance at New York City's Carnegie Hall this past April, RadicalMedia's filmed presentation of the immersive living space documentary, "We Chose to Go to the Moon," is finally available for the rest of us to watch. "We Chose to Go to the Moon" premieres Nov. 10 at 8:00 p.m. ET on PBS, PBS.org, and the PBS app, and we’ve got an exclusive clip to share featuring Mark and Kali Armstrong singing "Flight of Fancy." With a poignant introduction by Oscar winning director Ron Howard ("Apollo 13"), "We Chose to Go to the Moon" recalls the extraordinary saga of the global space race and Apollo moon landings by actors portraying pivotal persons who made it all happen. These roles include astronauts Neil Armstrong , Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins and Ed White, Mission Control trailblazer Poppy Northcutt, " Hidden Figures " mathematician Katherine Johnson and members of the spacefaring families that remained on Earth, including Janet Armstrong and Betty Grissom. This dynamic multimedia production is directed by Tony Award winner Michael Mayer ("Chess"), combining a unique fusion of theater, concert and documentary storytelling using rare archival footage alongside historic flags and artifacts taken to the Moon and returned home. It also revisits the ill-fated Apollo 13 mission and adds a special tribute to moonwalker Neil Armstrong performed by his son Mark and granddaughter Kali. "We Chose to Go to the Moon" is created, written and narrated by historian John Monsky and stars Ian Weinberger ("Hamilton"), Skylar Astin ("Pitch Perfect"), Brent Comer ("The Outsiders"), Claybourne Elder ("Company"), Elizabeth Gillies (Netflix's "Dynasty"), Taylor Louderman ("Mean Girls") and Joy Woods ("Galileo"). Finally, Ian Weinberger ("Chess," "Hamilton") pulls it all together by conducting Broadway vocalists and the Orchestra of St. Luke’s in a selection of popular period music showcasing songs such as "Fly Me to the Moon," "Rocket Man," "Space Oddity" and "Sound of Silence." We hope space fans around the world tune in to experience this sensational stage show that honors America's human spaceflight history!

item.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
item.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. Show And Availability Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. item.title: Camara reprimanded for 'clearly dangerous' impeding in Brazil practice
PyTorch 2.15 tackles the 'one bad GPU' problem
item.description: ML admins will be happy to learn that one bad GPU may no longer mean starting an entire training job from scratch. The latest 2.15 release of PyTorch includes a rewritten backend for Nvidia's Collective Communications Library (NCCL), designed to improve fault diagnosis and recovery when GPUs work together. This latest feature shows how its creators continue to advance the software from being a tool for researchers to being a cornerstone in production AI work. The interface to the networking library in PyTorch needed a rewrite – it was drowning in technical debt, said PyTorch core developer Tristan Rice , a Meta software engineer specializing in distributed computing, during a live YouTube livestream on Thursday. NCCL is pronounced "Nickel" and stands for the Nvidia Collective Communications Library. It provides PyTorch with a set of inter-GPU communication primitives, allowing GPUs to communicate within a single-node or across multi-node clusters, which is vital for running inference on large neural networks and for other tasks in building and maintaining LLMs. The old NCCL interface was too chaotic The previous PyTorch backend for NCCL, called ProcessGroupNCCL , could spawn dozens of communicators per process group, leading to intermittent deadlocks and unpredictable performance. The new version of the NCCL backend comes with a strict rule: One process group gets only one communicator during initialization. By default, this rule eliminates crosstalk between multiple communicators and all the complexities that entails. If a program requires parallelism, it will have to dispatch more process groups. The updated library also better handles stragglers by allowing for easier reconfiguration. If a GPU crashes or runs slowly, a third-party orchestrator can exclude the laggard and even assign a replacement worker. A “flight recorder” has also been added to give admins a better idea of what went wrong. Previously, if a cluster of GPUs stalled—perhaps from a timeout or deadlock—the user would just get a generic message. The new flight recorder captures all operations in a series of snapshots that can be inspected after a failure occurs. Rice noted the cleaned-up NCCL backend, also called ProcessGroupNCCL, will give developers a blank slate, making it easier to add new features. The legacy ProcessGroupNCCL is part of the 2.15 package as a rollback, but if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year. Nvidia origins Why, you may ask, does a machine learning framework need a specialized communications library? Like NumPy, PyTorch supports numerical computing, but it also provides tools for building and training neural networks on CPUs and GPUs. In these environments, workers must constantly exchange data such as tensors, gradients, activations, and weights. The standard TCP-based networking stack can introduce bottlenecks in large GPU clusters, so NCCL uses optimized communication

item.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . This post Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

item.title: The folks behind John Wick are back with Karōshi trailer
item.description: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun , as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. item.title: US air traffic control enters the 21st century, starts to abandon floppy disks
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration still uses computers that require floppy disks. But those are finally on the way out within the next few years. Yes, it’s still 2026, and yes, you read that right: The FAA – the agency responsible for overseeing aviation safety in the US – is finally getting rid of four systems dating back to the 1980s that remain in use at more than 400 facilities around the country, the agency announced on Thursday. “Good news America: floppy disks are out, 21st century tech is in,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in the FAA’s announcement. Only a few decades late, Sean, but we’re sure the flying public appreciates it. The new system, known as Enterprise Information Display System ( E-IDS ), is designed to consolidate data from various systems into a common digital platform, allowing air traffic controllers to access operational information and alerts needed to manage flights. E-IDS is replacing four legacy systems: Information Display System 4, used to track weather and operational info; the Automated Surface Observing System Controller Equipment Information Display System, which also relays weather information; the NAS Information Display System, which relays information about airports and other airspace conditions; and the En Route Information Display System (ERIDS), which handles information about flights. The FAA said E-IDS will improve how Pilot Reports and Notices to Airmen (NOTAMs) are collected and distributed. The agency has had its share of air traffic control SNAFUs, including one in 2023 that temporarily halted domestic flight departures nationwide after someone accidentally deleted a file from the NOTAM system. The FAA said it has already lined up five facilities to receive E-IDS upgrades: airports in Atlantic City, Nashville, and Rochester, New York, along with data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City. The agency plans to install the system at 435 sites by the end of 2028. That 2028 deadline echoes the ambitious three-year timetable Duffy laid out last year for overhauling the nation's air traffic control system. Aside from the four systems E-IDS will replace, the FAA has a lot of outdated technology, with the Government Accountability Office saying in 2024 that 51 of the agency’s 138 ATC systems were unsustainable due to lack of parts and funding to sustain or replace them. Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill allocated $12.5 billion for the FAA’s overhaul efforts, but that’s far short of what’s actually needed. In December of last year, the FAA said that it needed an additional $20 billion to handle upgrade costs, and that appears to still be the case. "To continue modernizing our air traffic control facility, Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford are calling on Congress to pass the Modern Skies Act," an FAA spokesperson told The Register in an email. That bill is asking for $30 billion to get ATC modernization across the finish line, the spokesperson added. " It will modernize our air traffi

item.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
item.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. Images make Andromeda look compact, but its full apparent extent is enormous — several times the width of the full moon — and our eyes usually pick up only the much brighter central region. Once you know that, the smudge starts making more sense. How and when I'm watching it Yo

item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. item.description: An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday . The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year. "Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease," Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. "Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family." The baby's death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday . The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. The state's explosive, ongoing measles outbreak has led to 1,467 cases so far this year. Read full article Comments

item.title: Mac lookalikes multiply as Linux raids Apple's wardrobe
item.description: Linux can do many things, but good looks aren't always its strong point. Apple has rather more of a reputation in that department, and a crop of new projects is bringing Mac-style polish to the open source desktop. Some are all-new, such as the Argentinian Lord OS , a whole new GUI desktop on top of Debian. Another, Cutefish , is a revival of a pre-ChatGPT project that never got as far as a complete release. Now it has version 1.0 for both x86-64 and Arm64, plus it's working on Mac binary compatibility via a work-in-progress layer called Reef . Ukrainian Desert OS is already at version 5.5 – practically a venerable elder in this company, despite appearing to be only about a year old. Meanwhile, ClokeOS uses Xfce for its desktop, but underneath, the OS is based on Apple's FOSS XNU kernel. The project lead plans to offer compatibility with multiple types of binaries: Linux apps, plus Mac apps via Darling , and Windows apps via Wine. This isn't new. Much as Cutefish has been revived, last year we reported on PearOS Linux , a very Mac-like skin on KDE Plasma. It has hooks in place for ambitious future features, such as Siri-style speech recognition. What's striking is the number of projects appearing and the pace of their development. Some offer both x86-64 and Arm64 builds, with Raspberry Pi editions in certain cases. For human coders, this would be months of hard work, but if it's just checking an additional box in an LLM development tool, then why wouldn't you? It's almost no extra work, but it widens the potential audience. Coveting Mac-like good looks is a longstanding urge among Linux users, and with legitimate reason. There's nothing wrong with Macs, even if you are mainly a FOSS user. Modern macOS, or OS X as it was called a decade ago, is a Unix underneath its shiny proprietary desktop, and many of the flagship Linux FOSS apps also have Mac versions, from Firefox and Thunderbird, via LibreOffice, to VirtualBox, plus less well-known but very handy apps such as Ferdium and Panwriter. We've written about the usefulness of FOSS apps on macOS before, including for reviving elderly Macs . Just a couple of months ago, we published a two-part guide on how to give Xfce a macOS-like layout and then how to tweak it so apps fit in better . We focused on the functionality, though, not the looks – we don't really care much for such things. If it does matter to you, though, you're not alone, and there are lots of themes and skins to make Xfce look prettier. Some of these are all-in-one packages that you can install on an existing distro to give it a new look. One recent example is Cupertino , developed with assistance from Claude. From a few years ago, there are Small Sur and Ventura-Xfce . From nine years ago, long pre-LLM, there is osXFCE . We can see the appeal. From 2006 to 2020, Macs used Intel x86 processors, and those machines are now all falling off the end of Apple support – only four Intel models supported last year's macOS 26 "Tahoe," support fo

item.title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. Yaroch’s conduct compromised multiple FBI investigations into criminal groups and nation-state adversaries, the office said, and it compromised FBI sources and methods used in fo

item.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
item.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. The researchers found that, in terms of detecting faint exoplanets, FLIP outperformed conventional image

Oak Ridge labs gets hybrid quantum-HPC system to test qubit error correction
item.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) now boasts a system for research into quantum error correction, combining IBM quantum processors with a high-performance compute (HPC) system based on AMD silicon. The Quantum Science Center ( QSC ) at ORNL, funded by the US Department of Energy (DoE), unveiled what it calls a co-design platform for quantum error correction, marrying up quantum and HPC technology. While useful, fault-tolerant quantum systems always seem to be at least a decade away, there have been notable advances over the past several years in the field of quantum error correction, according to ORNL. These include early demonstrations of protecting quantum information from environmental noise, which can cause loss of the fragile quantum states needed for computations. "Solving the challenges of quantum error correction is essential to making quantum computing a practical tool for scientific discovery, which is a priority for Oak Ridge National Laboratory," said QSC director Travis Humble. IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta said that it was no longer a question of whether error correction works, but how to accelerate and optimize error correction to build systems that scientists can use to tackle challenging problems. "This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale," he stated. ORNL's new tool combines an IBM Quantum System Two, equipped with the latest 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 quantum processors , and Umbra, a classical HPC system powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. According to AMD, the CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate everything, while the GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads. Also part of the system are AMD Versal SoCs to provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities for the quantum circuitry. ORNL says that this brings together the computing infrastructure needed for quantum error correction in a single environment, and opens it up to more researchers than ever before. They will use it to develop and validate quantum algorithms, workflows, and applications in an environment built for quantum-centric supercomputing, an emerging paradigm where quantum processors (QPUs), CPUs, and GPUs work together as one system. IBM says that one promising approach the co-design platform cloud explore is hierarchical error correction. It describes this as using an inner code to protect qubits within a module, while an outer code wraps around the inner code’s logical qubits and adds a second layer of protection. This approach could reach a trillion logical operations at a physical error rate of one in a thousand, IBM research suggested. item.title: RIP to the world’s ugliest car
item.description: Elon Musk has hit the brakes on the Cybertruck, announcing on X that Tesla will wind down production at its Texas factory around mid-2027. Despite years of delays , the stainless-steel turd Musk claimed was a futuristic, apocalypse-proof tank straight out of Blade Runner is headed for a production wind-down after roughly four years, putting the Cybertruck alongside such automotive flops as the Edsel and the DeLorean. We can’t even put the Cybertruck on the same tier as the Ford Pinto, as that deathtrap was produced for a decade. The first Cybertruck lumbered off Tesla’s production line in mid-2023 before going on sale later that year , and it was practically right out of the gate that the problems began. Within months of the first deliveries, recall notices began piling up on the monstrosity. Trim pieces were flying off, internal components were failing, cameras were malfunctioning – all in all, the thing has faced 11 recalls since hitting the road in late 2023, most recently in April 2026, when a defect in brake rotors was found to potentially cause cracks that could allow wheel studs to separate from their hubs. Musk had pinned a lot of Tesla's hopes on the Cybertruck a few years ago, describing it during the company's Q3 2023 earnings call as "a great product" that would eventually generate "significant positive cash flow" for Tesla. Musk said on that same earnings call that Tesla intended to ramp Cybertruck production up to 250,000 vehicles per year by 2025 to meet the over one million Cybertruck reservations he claimed Tesla had taken. Some Musk fans may still be waiting for their Cybertrucks, while others may have canceled their reservations after reading early reviews or experiencing the reality of driving such an ugly vehicle associated with a right-wing provocateur. Tesla hasn't disclosed how many reservations were canceled or converted into sales. Even then, it was widely reported in recent years that unsold Cybertrucks were piling up around the US, with Tesla unable to move them even with repeated price reductions. Tesla has never shared Cybertruck sales numbers, but it’s estimated that only around 70,000 of the things have been sold in the past three years - not exactly a ringing endorsement of its marketability. So that’s that for the Cybertruck - it’s safe to say it’s been a total disaster for Musk and Tesla. It never sold well, never became a boat , and will likely never be remembered fondly. ®

item.title: Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2% Strive reported $474.8 million of net income attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, a print that arrived Friday alongside a company claim that Class A total return had outperformed bitcoin by 103.7% year to date through the same date. GAAP net income was $509.0 million, or $5.24 a share on a fully diluted basis. Almost all of that came from a $533.7 million unrealized gain on digital assets marked to fair value. Operating revenue for the quarter was just $2.7 million, so the earnings line is a treasury mark, not a fee business. In a post on X that led with the outperformance figure, Strive also highlighted a year-to-date bitcoin yield of 63.2% and a bitcoin dollar gain of $9.00 per assumed diluted share outstanding, both measured through Sept. 30. Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole tied those metrics to the stock’s relative showing against the asset. “Strive has continued to successfully execute on its treasury management strategy, delivering a strong bitcoin yield year to date in 2026, which I believe is the primary driver of our common equity’s outperformance relative to Bitcoin so far this year,” Cole said in the earnings release. Bitcoin yield, buys and the preferred stack Bitcoin yield, as Strive defines it, is the percentage change in bitcoin per share over a period — not a cash yield. On that measure the company posted 18.5% in the third quarter alone and 19.3% from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30, after the SATS preferred debut. Strive acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter at an average cost of about $78,885 and 20,373 bitcoin over the nine months ended Sept. 30. Another 15,124 coins followed between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and 43,124 by Oct. 30, keeping Strive among the largest public corporate stacks after recent multi-thousand-coin buys and smaller weekly adds that still trailed Strategy . Digital assets at fair value were $2.34 billion on the Sept. 30 balance sheet. Cash had risen to $490.4 million by Oct. 30, and Strive still held Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred with a fair value of about $50.1 million. The capital stack that funded the buys is mostly perpetual preferreds. On Oct. 20 Strive closed a registered offering of 7 million shares of its 15% Series A perpetual preferred (SATS) for about $609 million in net proceeds. Preferred dividends of $34.2 million in the quarter are what turned the $509.0 million GAAP profit into the $474.8 million common figure. Strip the story to nine-month GAAP and the picture flips. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Strive posted a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $88.4 million. The third-quarter profit is real under fair-value accounting, but it is concentrated in one mark-to-market line. item.title: DoJ's 'Super Intelligence Task Force' up and running
item.description: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) says its Super Intelligence Task Force (SINTF) is now up and running, after president Donald Trump ordered the move in a memo last month. Headed up by director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, as well as associate attorney general Stanley Woodward and associate deputy attorney general Stephen Weiss, SINTF's responsibility is to protect the US's lead in artificial intelligence development. Thursday's announcement, which was littered with the " super intelligence " Trumpism, said the task force will ensure the US's SI/AI leadership remains uncompromised by foreign AI "abuse," including by state and state-backed groups, criminal enterprises, individuals, or corporate entities. Per Trump's October 13 memo [PDF], SITF will take "affirmative measures, as appropriate," to ensure the US stays ahead in AI development. It did not elaborate on what this nebulous phrase meant, but it can be reasonably assumed this means a breadth of proactive steps. The memo also stated that the task force will organize the DoJ's criminal and civil lawsuits involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities concerning public safety and AI misuse, develop prosecution guidance for unlawful AI conduct, and feed into legislative proposals to prevent "burdensome regulation." Addressing a Wall Street Journal tech conference this week, Pentagon CTO and SITF vice chair Emil Michael said the team would release details about its AI regulatory landscape later this month. The task force will also shoulder various cross-departmental responsibilities, such as "deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters" among departments and the offices of US attorneys. According to quotes from senior officials, chief among the concerns facing ordinary US citizens are AI attacks that target individuals, as well as those that aim to disrupt critical infrastructure and other national security interests. "The creation of the DOJ-SITF marks an important moment for the Department to help advance SI technologies and, at the same time, protect American innovation," said Weiss. "The Department also has a responsibility to utilize law enforcement tools at our disposal to deter improper use of SI, harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended. The Department is committed to protecting all Americans and our business interests." Trump compelled the US to start using the term "super intelligence" in September, claiming "artificial intelligence," the widely used and original term coined in the mid-1950s, was a better descriptor for the technology's capabilities. The US government's dedicated website for SI states that "America is in a race for Super Intelligence. We intend to win it." It also highlights a number of initiatives the government has taken to promote its AI supremacy, including legal guidance to streamline federal approvals, leading to more data centers being
